Monday! How is it already Monday?




(adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});
 Are you like me in that you say things like, “oh, it’ll be so nice when summer dies down–I’ll have so much more free time! Life will stop moving so fast!” only to then start saying, “ohh after the holidays! It’ll be so nice then!” (Do we ever stop saying this? I swear life hasn’t stopped moving any less quickly!) I remember when we walked into our room in Mexico, running out to the balcony, giddy over the view and the weather screaming “I CAN’T BELIEVE WE’RE HEEEREEE!!”–I stopped to take a mental picture and remember how I felt in that moment, because I knew in a blink, the trip would be over. And that’s pretty much how it went! But luckily, I have all these great photos to remember it by, right? We snapped these our second day (our first full day, if you will) in Cancun. We were still getting our bearings around the resort–we stayed at Secrets Playa Mujeres, and it was a dream (full review on our trip and the resort right over here!) There was this beautiful boardwalk that took you from the hotel down to the beach. We were like giddy little teenagers walking around and taking in how beautiful it was. We hadn’t explored that side of the resort yet, and just around the bend, we saw a little tiki bar with swings, and about a dozen cabanas to the left. (More on the cabanas in the next post–we had slept in too late to snag one that day!) I then witnessed another girl ordering something called a “Bahama Mama,” at the tiki bar, and she was promptly handed the most beautiful peachy-coral colored drink. (Which happened to be the EXACT color of the dress I was wearing!) I decided that I had to have one. What else could you want at 10am in Mexico? I’m never usually one for tropical, girly drinks, but something about being in Mexico changed my mind. I think I racked up Bahama Mamas in the double digits while I was there! This dress is the perfect tropical vacation dress. I wore it here as a beach cover-up (how cute would it look with these wrap-around sandals?) but you could easily pair it with espadrille wedges like these for a dinner date! (We loved that the resort had a bunch of restaurants, many of them more upscale, which was nice to have an excuse to dress up for dinner, rather than living in flip flops the whole time!) Shop all dress colors:   Afterwords, we headed to brunch, and then got lucky enough to snag two beach chairs right by the infinity pool, overlooking the beach! (Heaven.) To be honest, I always thought I would get bored on an all-inclusive vacation–but I was so, so wrong. If you’re like me, I will assure you, there are so many things to do at the resort and in Cancun in general, you will never be bored! (Also, I surprised myself–ALL I wanted to do was lay on the beach and do nothing, haha!)     
  Fast forward to now–you know, real life–I have to admit my brain is still in post-holiday/vacation mush. I hope this week will be more productive! Do you feel back to normal yet? We had a very relaxing and fun weekend! We hadn’t hung out with Kelly and Mitch in FOREVER. Since before the holidays! (So yes, essentially, forever.) We went over there on Friday night and had so much fun. (Emma has grown soooo much since we last saw her. Can’t she stay tiny forever?!) I made skinny pool dip (recipe here, but I hold the black olives. Bleh!) asian turkey sliders (which I don’t have a recipe for because I usually make up my own!) and coleslaw! Kelly made fruit salad. (That means wine. Shhhh.) It seems like it’s been forever since I cooked anything, so it felt so good to get back in the kitchen! (Speaking of kitchens, did you see our latest kitchen update?)

Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog November 22, 2016   OUTFIT: Red Sweater: VERY old, but similar here, here, here (only $55!) and here (total steal at $39!) // Ballet Flats: Repetto, bought in Paris, but very similar versions here (patent red) and here (non patent red). They also come in EVERY color and are so, so comfortable! I want a pair in light pink, and also like the one’s with the midi heels. Jeans: Levi’s (similar styles here, and here!) // Scarf: Old, but similar here, here, and here. (We also have a whole plaid scarf page in our Winter Guide!) // BEAUTY: MAC lip primer + lipstick in “Diva,” Estee Lauder eyebrow pencil (LOVE that thing!) and blush,  Dior Mascara, Bareminerals Complexion Rescue + Mineral makeup foundation, hair curled with a Beachwaver curling iron & Oribe dry texture spray.    Want to know what’s really fun?  Discovering an old staple in the back of your closet, and finding something different to wear it with that makes it feel brand new again.  That’s what happened with this red sweater! (Mine is old, but similar version here). It’s been my go-to for countless holiday parties, Christmas mornings, Christmas Eves–you name it. Plus, it’s the prettiest shade of punchy read, so it obviously works great for non-holiday occasions too!  Speaking of holiday go-tos, having great festively colored staples is great to fall back on, but sometimes they can leave your outfit feeling old and stale. Like, “I’m wearing this, but I don’t LOVE wearing this” kind of attitude, you know? Sometimes all it takes is a little remixing! I made a few simple swaps and made this feel like a completely brand new outfit. First, instead of wearing it with the typical boots, I went for a red on red look by choosing ballet flats instead. Sounds simple, but results in a whole different look altogether! If you followed along on my Paris posts, you’ll know that I got these adorable little red ballet flats while we were on our trip there. They are seriously the BEST flats I’ve ever worn–so comfortable and feel like you’re pretty much barefoot. Repetto is the brand who makes them, which apparently is THE place to get flats if you’re a French girl. They actually make REAL ballet shoes (like for real ballerinas! How cool is that?) I get so much joy every time I put them on, remembering what an incredible trip we had. I think classic items of clothing and accessories are some of the best souvenirs you can buy. They allow you to re-live your trip for years to come each time you wear them! (Same goes with my leather jacket my mom bought me as a gift when she came to visit me while studying abroad in Italy!)  Okay…back to the “easy wardrobe swaps” conversation. Another one I made: instead of my dark skinnies, I pulled some classic mom-style jeans (side note, I’m pretty sure my mom had this EXACT pair of jeans when I was growing up, I remember them so vividly! Mom jeans in the most literal sense.) My trick for making boxy sweaters flattering: style them with high-waisted jeans. Go for a half-tuck or side-tuck, which defines your waist and makes you feel more feminine and less like a shoebox ;-P (Who wants to feel like a shoebox?!)  The final touch? A classic plaid scarf (which also had red in it) and swipe of deep, dark red lipstick. (Red is clearly the underlying theme here, have you noticed?) Sometimes the matchy-matchy thing is the best. “How easy is that?” (I’m basically the Barefoot Contessa of outfit remixing. Not really.)

Get this widget. Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog July 31, 2018  Happy Tuesday! I am admittedly still recovering from my bestie Melissa’s bachelorette party ? BUT we were up bright and early yesterday to fly to Cincinnati for the week! I’m tagging along on Neal’s work trip (we have the Southwest companion pass, so I can hop on any flight of his for free) because my best friend lives here–we’ll be road tripping to Lexington to visit our friend Nancy (she’s basically our second mom) and stay there for the night. I basically spent the entirety of yesterday working on this post–I get so many questions about my favorite bras and underwear but it is truly not a one-size-fits-all answer! Every woman’s body is SO different–so, instead of doing a post on just MY favorites, I thought it would be WAY better to ask all of you guys!  I took to Instagram to ask your recommendations and got absolutely flooded with responses! I spent hours pouring over them, tallying up the most popular answers, and hand selecting the best quotes about them that I thought best described why they were so great, what body types and lifestyles they’re good for! I know I personally got a lot of recommendations I can’t wait to try! Read below for our fellow GG community members favorite bras, undies, and why they love them so much! (Please note, if your Instagram handle doesn’t say your real name, I just used the first initial of your Instagram handle, haha!)  I have to say, I was so excited to come across reader Bri’s incredibly thorough response–she was a certified bra specialist through Nordstrom–so she’s basically our #1 expert here. I thought it was best to start with her advice first and foremost! Bri says… “First of all, 80% of women are in the wrong bra size. and it’s so hard to name one brand that is perfect for every woman because everyone is so different. Some of my favorite brands are Natori, Chantelle, and Wacoal because they have a large range of sizes for every woman!”  Bri also recommends getting fitted at Nordstrom because I think they have the most accurate sizes. “Even if you don’t want to buy anything, you can still get fitted for free! It will change your life to wear a correctly sized bra!” she gushes.  That being said, a lot of you RAVED (and I mean RAVED) about those exact brands she mentioned–plus, a few more as well! Let’s jump into details! This was easily the #1 most recommended brand by woman of all cup sizes–I’d say if you’re looking for a non wireless bra, this is probably where I’d recommend you start, based on all of your feedback! Plus, a lot of their bras are part of the Nordstrom Anniversary Sale (which is only going for a few more days!) Bri says, “Natori feathers bra is great and it’s always part of Nordstrom’s Anniversary Sale! It’s deep v plunge/ life bra with lace for those who are wearing a deep v dress or top that wants a little lift. I’s always such a beautiful bra and it comes in a variety of colors.”  “A” emphatically agrees– “Natori bras are the best thing EVER. I’m a 34C and adore the Everyday T-shirt bra, and so do both my sister and mom! It’s the perfect comfy bra for basically everything (except tops with a super deep v or low armholes) with no show through and just the right amount of support.”  Rachel adds, “I love the Natori feathers bras–they are so pretty with light coverage (I don’t need much!) Jen echoes the resounding praise for Natori bras and adds another huge plus: “they hold their shape wash after wash!” Aerie also gave Natori a run for its money–I’ve heard really great things about them before, but I was very excited to hear that even larger chested ladies found their bralettes to be supportive enough–which isn’t something you hear too often! If you’ve been wanting a “barely there” bra–I’d start here! “I love bralettes from Aerie–I usually wear a medium top but have a larger chest and the large size works great for me. They are comfortable and super cute. Not as supportive as a regular bra but I still wear them all the time. The brand also stands for body positivity which is great and they’re on sale all the time”–Sheila  “I’m very small chested (barely a B and only reached it after age 25!) and love Aerie for bralettes. I don’t need support, so anything that feels as little like a bra as possible is what I am for. I particularly like their unlined and unpadded bras (also confirming your recent discovery that American Eagle actually has some really cute stuff!!” -Liz “Aerie is great for girls with small frames–they have a 30 band and are cheap!” –Kate “I love the Aerie Real Me bras–I have a large bust and they are comfy without looking huge!”–Elisabeth Bri says, “Chantelle is one of my favorite brands because of the wide range of sizes. They go from A-H and have push-ups and full coverage.”  Reader Yvonne also agrees– “Chantelle bras are great for bustier girls bc the underwear support is awesome. No extra padding, and they’re still pretty which is rare for larger sizes! I love the Rive Gauche bra, which I got during last year’s NSale–it’s on sale again right now!” One of Bri’s all-time favorite brands, “Typically for us bustier women, there’s not a lot of cute options. It’s either old lady minimizers or zero coverage support/cute bras. Freya is a European company that offers super cute options for those of us with big boobs. This happened so often where a young woman would come in and say, “I know there’s nothing cute in my size…” (many of which had been told this at Victoria’s Secret) and I would always pull Freya and they would be amazed!”  Readers like Kate also agree– “Freya is a great brand for small rib cages and large boobs!”  What seems to me to be a big Third Love rival–I had always wondered about this brand so I’m so glad a few of you weighed in on it and had great things to say. Granted, ThirdLove was a more popular recommendation, but people specifically called out Lively for their wireless bra and strapless bra! “The strapless bra is life-changing”–Megan “I recently ordered a wireless bra and bralette from Lively after doing a LOT of research.” –Emily “Cute, well-priced and non under-wire options for us ladies with surgeries up top!”–Jess “Never going back to underwire! I’m smaller, but they cater to most sizes!”–J Another that get’s the bra specialist stamp of approval! It sounds like these are an absolute must for anyone who struggles to find a good supportive bra for larger chests.  Shelby says, “I received the Wacoal “Embrace Lace” bralette as a gift from one of my bridesmaids at my bachelorrete and I LOVE IT. I’m normally a 34DD so bralettes don’t usually come to mind for me but the bio wire is so comfortable and I still feel supported (and it’s cute!) The downside is that the lace is hard to wear under some t-shirts but I still wear it all the time. I have the black and I’m hoping to purchase the beige soon. Can also be made into a racer back!” Preeti sings Wacoal’s praises–“I’m a 36DD and always used to get VS but they’d push me up so much my cleavage would be at my chin! Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog November 10, 2017  Wahoo! Can you believe today’s post marks month TWO of the Capsule Wardrobe Remix series?! Hooray! If you didn’t catch it earlier, I debuted this series last month to help you get more out of your current wardrobe, fill holes in your closet, and to spark creativity when putting together your everyday outfits. October’s series was a hit (click here to see October’s capsule wardrobe item list) and I showed you how to style leather leggings three ways, four ways to wear a black dress from work to the weekend, four ways to wear a convertible sweater, and finally, last week, four versatile ways to wear boyfriend jeans! Now, what’s up this month? Let’s find out! What has changed, and what is different? You guys asked for more outfits that could work in and out of the office. (Especially those in the business casual environment.) –Check! You asked for staples that could be go-to’s as we ramp up for the holidays, but not so festive that you won’t be able to wear them after December–check! You asked for more ideas on how to style your knee-high and over the knee boots–check! You asked for ideas on how to wear your Barbour Beadnell jackets–when I asked which one, it was SUCH a half and half split, that I decided to throw both of them in there. Does this mean I think you NEED both jackets? Of course not! Remember, I want you take what works for you from this series, and leave what doesn’t. Do I think you’ll get a ton of wear if you own both jackets? Of course! Above all, if you’re looking to fill some holes in your closet this season, I hope this post right here can become a go-to wardrobe planner for you. Now–shall we get into the list of this month’s items? YAS!  I recently got this camel coat from Ann Taylor and I am absolutely loving it! I’m confident that it will be one of my most favorite purchases of the entire season. It’s beautiful, chic, and most importantly–warm! I’ve been wearing it non-stop lately, and it’s even warm enough to still remain your “going out coat” all winter when you’re all dressed up and need a coat to go with your pretty dress. (Obviously not for trekking through snow in the daytime, that is a job for Canada Goose, but we don’t need puffers in a capsule wardrobe now do we? ?) My Barbour coats are some of the most functional things I own, aside from being super stylish! If you’re wondering if they’re worth the money–they 100% are. They are both extremely well-made and will last a lifetime. Again, you guys requested BOTH of these so much that I normally would not have put both coats in here (granted, I don’t know which one I would’ve picked because they’re so different!) What I love about the waxed beadnell is that it’s truly an all-weather coat. It’s water and wind resistant, and you can also purchase a liner (this one is fleece-lined!) and hood to go with it for added warmth! In terms of function, I prefer this Beadnell over it’s quilted counterpart because of the flannel-lined hand warming pockets and the ability to add the snap-on hood. The warming pockets are super deep and have a unique curve to them so your hands stay SO toasty warm with no cold air leaking in. When I wear it, I don’t even wear gloves, because that’s how warm they keep my hands! It comes in several colors, which I’ll link in the widget below! Shop Waxed Barbour Beadnell coats:    Where to buy: My recommended places to purchase Barbour are Tuckernuck and Nordstrom, but they are sold a lot of different places! I would check both of these because they tend to stock different sizes/colors at certain times. Sizing: they used to run REALLY small (b/c European sizes) but I think they’ve updated their sizing now–from what I can tell, the reviews mention to size up for a more relaxed fit if you want more room for layers. They don’t run as small as the quilted versions do. The Waxed Beadnell’s brother, the Quilted Beadnell, is also in a totally different league in terms of style! If you love the classic, preppy, quilted look but don’t want to pay an arm and a leg for a Burberry quilted jacket, this could be a good option! Granted, it’s not completely comparable, because of the corduroy collar, it’s a bit more casual, but still–a great dupe if I say so! I love that you can turn up the sleeves and have the plaid underneath as well! This version has a polar quilt lining, so it’s also extremely warm! You can also purchase a liner to go underneath this one as well for extra warmth. This one also comes in several colors, which I’ll link in the widget below. Shop Quilted Barbour Beadnell coats:    Where to buy: My recommended places to purchase Barbour are Tuckernuck and Nordstrom, but they are sold a lot of different places! I would check both of these because they tend to stock different sizes/colors at certain times. Sizing: Run small, size up. I’m wearing a US4 and I usually wear an XS in jackets. Chunky cardigans are really in right now, and I’ve received quite a few questions on what to wear them with OTHER than just jeans or leggings, so I thought this would be a fun challenge to tackle! The cardigan I’ve featured here has sadly since sold out in this particular color but I’m linking similar versions in the widget below (most of these come in several different colors!):   Probably my #1 most worn piece in my winter wardrobe is a thin striped turtleneck. (I also have it in grey and wear that one frequently as well!) It’s a super thin material, so it’s really more of a cozy version of a t-shirt. These make the best base layers and I wear them under everything for both visual interest as well as warmth. If stripes aren’t your thing, they come in lot’s of other colors too!   Arguably one of my favorite items in this capsule–I am in love with this camisole and have worn it so many times since I purchased it a few weeks ago. It looks amazing under chunky cardigans, paired with skirts, jeans–whatever. It’s one of Neal’s favorite things I’ve bought in a LONG time. (He says its one of the few things I own that a Grandma wouldn’t wear.)   I’ve had this silk button-down (also available at Nordstrom–they also have a short sleeve version!) for what feels like forever, and it’s rare for a week to go by without me pulling it out of the closet. I actually wrote a whole post about how much I love it right over here! It’s perfect for work (you can wear a nude bra underneath with no show-through, or a nude cami, if you’d prefer) and for date night, I love wearing a black lace bralette underneath (it’s not see through-just a hint!) OR you could even wear the lace camisole underneath! Basically, its my go-to top year-round for pretty much all occasions, and it’s a really great price too!   I chose a camel crewneck sweater here because they are so great for layering and I chose a camel color scheme here because it goes with everything and I think it just makes you look so chic. Any other color would be great here too, it just depends on your preference–the key is just that it’s crewneck! I wear one often with my striped tissue turtleneck underneath, or even the silk button down! It also looks super cute layered over dresses or tucked into skirts.   Another sweater that makes me feel incredibly chic and timeless–mine is old from (shocker) Everlane, but this black turtleneck is very similar, as is this one! It’s flattering, slimming and can be dressed up or dressed down very easily! Black sweaters are also key for travel–they don’t show any dirt, stains or spills!   It’s OFFICIALLY almost the holidays–which means…ba da daaa! Time to break out the plaid! I love this skirt by BB Dakota because it’s festive, but not TOO festive to where to feels “Christmassy”–which means, you can totally wear it after the holidays, too. It is TO DIE with OTK boots, but can also work for the office with a pair of tights and pumps! It runs quite large, so size down! (I’m wearing a size 0) If you want something a little less “plaidish” there’s also this really cute grey windowpane wrap skirt! I plan to feature this skirt by sharing how to style a plaid skirt four ways, so get excited! I present to you–the ONLY dress you need to buy this season! (That is, if you only wanted to buy one dress.) It’s made by Everlane and comes in dark green, black, and a beautiful dark red hue. “Sleeveless?” you might be thinking, “for winter?” But here’s the thing: with sleeveless dresses, you can layer long sleeves underneath for a completely new look! For a more formal occasion, wear it sleeveless with your best pair of pretty earrings and some beautiful pumps! (And drape the camel coat over your shoulders–you’ll look like a million bucks!) This dress can be dressed up for a winter wedding or holiday party, or dressed down with boots for brunch. The opportunities are endless, really. I am absolutely loving it and have worn it so many ways this season already! See how to style this holiday dress four ways.   Do you know what ponte pants are? If you don’t, you might want to sit down, because your mind is about to be BLOWN. They’re essentially fancy leggings (made with sturdier, nicer fabric) you can wear to the office, but also wear out to dinner, on the airplane, or literally anywhere because they’re so dang comfy. Yeah–amazing. I know you guys were wanting more business-casual looks, so I had to include these! I love this pair because they have the seam in the front and the legs aren’t QUITE as skinny/tight as leggings, so they are extra appropriate if you work in an office. They also come in charcoal. Such a great price too–under $50!  See how to wear ponte pants four ways. Of course, I had to throw one pair of jeans in here! I always recommend high-waisted, dark skinny jeans. They’re not just the most flattering–but they’re also the most versatile. You can get away with dark skinnies just about anywhere outside of a wedding. I love both the Rag & Bone Skinny Jeans (33% off right now!) that I featured in last month’s capsule and the J.Brand Maria jeans (many pairs also 30% off!) which I’ll be wearing this month! The crown jewel of my wardrobe: my Stuart Weitzman Lowland boots. I wear them SO. MUCH. And sadly, I can confidently say there is no budget-friendly duplicate out there. I have searched high and low! They are expensive for a reason–no other thigh-high, tie-in-the-back boots that I’ve found really hug your leg like these do. However–good news–I DO love the budget-friendly Blondo Olivia boots! They don’t look exactly the same, (they aren’t as tall, and they stretch in the back vs. tie) but if you want a boot that is going to hug your leg in a similar fashion, this is a great choice! They’re also waterproof, and come in grey as well! I wear these boots when I want to save my Stuart Weitzmans from crazy weather! I just recently got these knee-high boots from Splendid (you saw me style them over here!) and I absolutely love the look of them. They look so cute with skirts and dresses as well as jeans! Best of all, they are SO comfy. I walked all over San Francisco in them one day and zero blisters or toe pinching! They come in black as well as brown–Sam Edelman makes a similar pair in a lighter tan color that is beautiful as well! Linking more below as well:   Another item from Everlane (they are really the MVP brand of this capsule!) I got these oxfords last spring and wore them all the way through May–and I was SO excited to pull them out again for fall! They’re truly one of the most beautifully crafted pair of shoes that I own. I love that they’re so classic and preppy looking, but the slightly pointed toe provides a more modern, minimalistic twist.   They’re back again! Yes, you also saw them in last month’s capsule, but you know the saying–if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it! Every woman should have one pair of classic, sleek, black pumps. I adore these Sam Edelmans. (Mine are actually slinkbacks from a few years ago but these are the current version. There is also a version with an ankle strap!) The price point on these is great, they are super comfy, and they are so versatile, you will wear them year-round from everything from work to weddings to dates and everything in between.   Ah, yes, you will recognize some more old friends from October’s capsule wardrobe! My handbags stayed the same, well, because I really don’t own that many handbags, and I still believe these are three of the most versatile bags you can own! I love this leopard clutch and wear it everywhere. (Nordstrom actually has a TON of different leopard clutches right now!) I’m a huge fan of it for going out because it brightens up even the most basic outfit. Plus, it’s such a steal for less than $50 and it looks and feels like the designer version.  The Madewell Transport tote making the capsule wardrobe cut comes as a shock to absolutely none of you, I am sure. It’s my everything bag. Work, travel, groceries–whatever, this is always the bag I’m reaching for and it comes in several sizes, styles and colors as well.   I was so on the fence when I purchased this crossbody (it’s Rebecca Minkoff’s ‘Love’ bag in size small!) as to whether or not I would wear it, but I’d have to say it’ snow become one of my most reached for bags. I really love the fact that it’s olive, which is a neutral, but a really fun mix-up from the typical tan or grey. Although my exact version is no longer available, this one is nearly identical, just slightly larger!   I chose this scarf because it’s neutral (so it goes with everything) but also has a pattern for added interest. Plus, you can wear it SO many different ways–it can be a wrap or poncho, too! Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog July 26, 2017   Before we got engaged, I hardly ever entertained the idea of an at-home workout. Let’s be honest, physical activity is not my idea of a good time, so without the whole “wedding workout” motivation, the only way I could get into working out was if someone was telling me what to do the entire time. You guys already know how much I love Corepower (I wrote about that here!) But sometimes I just don’t have enough time to spare to get into the studio, therefore, my only option is something quick that I can execute in my living room. I’ve tried workout videos, but those are just downright boring, so I prefer something that I can do while I’m watching TV. (Is it ironic that I like to watch Barefoot Contessa reruns while doing squats?) There are two workouts that really stand out when I need to squeeze in a quick workout. If you often find yourself in the same situation–I can’t recommend these enough!  Blair got me hooked on BBG awhile back, and I fully vouch that it WORKS. After the first couple of weeks doing BBG a few times per week, even Neal was like, “WOAH! That works!” The program is made to follow each day, but I usually only do it a couple of times per week in between yoga and I’ve seen great results. The moves are really simple and doable at home. They sometimes call for weights or a bench, but I don’t even own those! (On several occasions I’ve used a stack of coffee table book for weighted squats and a dining chair for step-ups in lieu of a bench, haha!) The workouts are essentially made up of two different circuits, and each day focuses on a different group of muscles. Each circuit is timed–7 minutes each, then repeat one more time through–28 minutes total! It’s a great workout for a lunch break too–you could totally do it in your office, or even outside in a park!  Okay, this is my absolute FAVORITE workout. …forrrr the sole reason that it only lasts for 7 minutes  This is a good workout for when you’re feeling all, “My life is in shambles and there is absolutely ZERO WAY I can work out today.” (Guess what: You cannnnn!) Who doesn’t have 7 minutes? Honestly it’s not even long enough to sweat, so if you’re in a pinch and need to get out the door, you can even get by without showering! While this workout is short, it’s definitely not easy. I use an app called “Wahoo Seven Minutes” and it essentially times you and walks you through each move–30 seconds of going as hard as you can, with 10 seconds of rest in between. It’s pretty genius!     Have you guys heard of Outdoor Voices? They’re an awesome athletic clothing brand that makes the CUTEST stuff. It’s all really well made and super comfortable! (And no, this isn’t sponsored, I just LOVE them so much!) The material is substantial, so there’s no risk of show-through (plus, it sucks you in and hides everything you want to be hidden, if you know what I mean! :-P) Whenever I need motivation to work out, I pull on this crop top (c/o) and it’s so darn cute, I can’t not get excited about it! The cropped quality always really helps in hot yoga, too–the less material–the better! I also opted for these high waisted leggings (c/o) which I love because they have a hidden pocket for my credit card, ID, and key! The fabric that they use on all of their items is four way stretch, and it does a great job of wicking away sweat! Both items run pretty true to size as well! After that, I was burnt out on the color, deciding it was for little girls. Now, fast forward later in life, it’s become one of my favorite colors again. Often people think it’s just for spring and summer, but who says fall outfits can’t be girly? If you’re like me and scared of feeling too bubblegum barbie–go with softer pink hues like blush, which feel more subdued and sophisticated. Light pink is such a flattering color on everybody! Also, if you don’t own a pair of great nude pumps, I would highly recommend it! Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog February 20, 2015   Dress: Kate Spade (old, similar below!) // Jacket: Old, similar below // Booties: Pour La Victoire // Knee socks: Forever 21 // Bracelets: J.Crew and SeeSong designs fishtail bracelet // Ring: Nordstrom Rack (old, similar here) I’m not sure about you, but I’ve been getting very antsy with my closet lately. Despite the fact that it’s still sub zero outside, I’m telling myself that spring is just around the corner, so I’m starting to mix in some spring items for the sake of my own sanity. One of the things I like to do is rotate a spring dress into my arsenal. Styled with the right pieces, it adds just the amount of cheer to brighten your winter day, without being total spring overkill.  



(adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});
    Pull some of your favorites out of your closet and play around with them. The trick is to just make sure it’s “layerable,” that is, have a silhouette that allows for layers to be added without it looking bulky or frumpy. For example, if this dress flared out at the sides, it would look like I was 10 pounds heavier by wearing this jacket. But if the jacket was cropped, that would look much better! Tighter fitting dresses often work better in this case, OR you can add a belt to create a more defined waistline. One of my favorite ways to sneak in some extra warmth is to add a turtleneck underneath (which you all know by now). Just make sure the neckline allows for you to do so. This dress looked weird with a turtleneck because it has a high V neckline. If you want to layer a turtleneck under, scoop necklines are the most foolproof. So, in this case, since the “under” was out, I went with layering “over” and adding a classic, black leather jacket. (Which you can never go wrong with!) Granted, I still need a heavy coat over it to go outside, but that’s okay. Layers, remember? An easy way to tone down the springy factor in pretty much anything is to pair it with edgier pieces. Here, the leather jacket and booties work together to accomplish this, but it can also work with a punky handbag, or jewelry as well. You don’t get much wear out of those booties when it’s 90 degrees outside! Often times, booties=winter, so wear your flirty floral number with boots now, and then swap them for feminine sandals later. Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog February 6, 2019  Hii guys!  So I was perusing the internet last night, doing my usual stalking, when I came across LOFT’s website. (I think I got an email about their 40% off sale). Now, I’m not usually a big LOFT shopper. I think most of their stuff is great for work but obviously I don’t work in a traditional work environment so I don’t really need any of that stuff. I also feel like I’ve happened to come across their selection at times where I didn’t see anything I liked–very hit or miss–so this particular retailer is not usually top of mind for me.  BUT as I was perusing, to my surprise, I loved SO MANY THINGS. I went on stories and asked, “GUYS. Should I be shopping at LOFT more?! Have I been living under a rock!?” 72% of you said YES–and many of you who said no said you would still be interested in seeing my picks ?So…here we are! SO many of you raved about their selection of items that are perfect for the office, yet cute enough to wear outside of work. It’s also fantastic that they sell both petite and plus sizes, and that their items are on-trend but not trendy, so you don’t feel like they go out of style.  I heard a lot of mixed things about quality, especially in regards to pants–saying they bag out. Bummer! But I have heard good things from you about their Ponte Pants, so I think it’s kind of a trial and error sort of thing and may depend on the style.  I heard a lot of feedback saying their stuff doesn’t hold up in the wash, BUT–big tip–I think a big part of this probably has to do with how you’re washing your clothes. I agree that it’s not say, Everlane quality, but we all know that already! The stuff I have bought from LOFT isn’t any lower quality than say, Topshop or Zara–so I think this has more to do with proper care vs. quality.  Blouses, sweaters, and dainty dresses should be always be hand washed in cold or warm water (It’s really easy to do in the sink–just let them soak–or throw them all in the bathub ?) Or, if you’re short on time, you can also wash them on the most gentle cycle possible, in a lingerie bag. Then, hang them or lay them flat to dry on a towel. Also, just wash things as little as possible–not after every wear. Washing them wears them out and ruins them, so only wash your stuff if it’s truly dirty. This should help your clothes (LOFT or not) last longer! Read my laundry post on how to stop ruining all your clothes right here!  Okay, that all being said, here are some really cute picks that I LOVED from LOFT’s new arrivals! They are all super versatile, you can wear them for work or outside of work, now and well into spring! Plus, tops and sweaters are all 40% off! I’m curious to know what you think–which of these items would you like to see me style?   Striped Cardigan:  This might be my favorite thing on the whole list. I don’t have a lot of button-front cardigans and I’ve been looking to add more to my wardrobe. They’re cute layered, they’re cute all by themselves buttoned up! I absolutely love this one. You can wear it with jeans or wear it with work pants to the office! 40% off!  The Perfect LBD:  Every so often, I stumble upon a universally flattering dress on tons of different shapes and sizes that is perfect for all occasions (in and outside of the office) and seasons. This dress is one of them! It’s so cute, and you can layer a collared shirt or turtleneck under it right now for colder months! (See how to do that in this post!) Chambray bow blouse:  I am a sucker for a good bow top, and like pretty much everything at LOFT, it’s perfect for work, but something you’ll wear a ton outside of work too.  I love that it’s a light chambray–which mixes up the texture! Wear it with: a skirt or ponte pants for the office, a pair of white jeans and a trench coat for a springy weekend look, or a skirt and OTK boots! Springy sweater #1:  LOFT has a lot of really adorable sweaters right now that are perfect for spring. (I.E. You can wear them now because it’s still cold, but you can FEEL like you’re out of your winter wardrobe slump!) I particularly love this one for it’s pretty intricate details–comes in more colors, too! 40% off!  Travel wrap:  I always advocate traveling with a wrap! They come in so handy on airplanes, trains, you can ball them up and use them as a pillow, they make a casual outfit look more polished–it’s hard to beat this price! 30% off!  Striped Midi Dress:  Midi dresses are SO wonderful–you never have to worry about flashing someone when you bend over, a gust of wind coming up at an inopportune moment–you get the picture. This one is casual, but so easy to dress up. Wear it now with booties (tights optional) and wear it later with your favorite heels, flats, or classic sneakers! There are infinite ways you can wear this one. Leopard skirt:  I will say this about LOFT mini skirts–I very much appreciate that they are short enough to not look frumpy, but just long enough to get away with wearing them to places like the office, lunch with grandma, etc. Those are hard to find! This is one of them. I fell in LOVE with the leopard print, and while yes, it’s a little louder than a typical “statement” piece–but that doesn’t mean it’s not super versatile. Wear it outside of work with OTK boots, your favorite heels, and a moto jacket! Striped turtleneck:  I couldn’t NOT include the on-sale striped turtleneck–because who couldn’t use another one in their reserves? I love how this one is ribbed, so it’s a little different than a turtleneck t-shirt! 40% off!  Easy peplum blouse:  This blouse looks like it could be from Sezane or Anthropologie–I absolutely love how beautiful and feminine it is! Definitely something you’ll wear throughout the spring and summer, but you can totally wear it now with a leather or suede jacket thrown over the top, and your favorite neutral booties! 40% off!  Little red skirt:  I MEAN? I want this red skirt immediately so I can wear it with sweet ballet flats and feel like Madeline. Or something. It’s a statement while being classic and preppy at the same time. It will look LOVELY with a trench coat for spring! Tweed shift dress:  Another amazing work dress that looks 600x more expensive than it is. I’ve been really into tweed lately. And by lately, I mean I haven’t really purchased anything tweed yet, but yesterday I decided that I really wanted to. ?This is the perfect piece for now and later. Get some inspiration in this post “How to wear a shift dress” for how to wear it tons of ways! Tweed mini:  Ah, the tweed parade continues. Again, the perfect skirt length–not too short, not too long–if you’re going for a classic/preppy Parisian look–you’ll be all about this skirt. I am itching to wear it with my cap toe pumps!  Springy sweater #2:  Similar to the sweater above, but a little bit different! I love it in white–it’s a staple you’ll wear over and over again through spring, and for years to come. Another versatile piece that you can wear for work and with jeans, shorts, skirts, etc! 40% off!  Reversible sweater coatigan:  I am in love with this easy sweater coat! First of all, it’s reversible, and second, you can wear it with literally everything. Keep it on the back of your chair at work, wear it when you travel, wear it to brunch with leggings and sneakers, wear it to yoga–whatever! It instantly polishes up your outfit, and is way more chic than a sweatshirt! 40% off!  Filed Under: Jess' Picks, Style

 There are so many areas of Chicago that really come alive this time of year! One of my all-time favorite places is Oak Street in the Gold Coast. It’s a street near and dear to my heart–I used to live just a few blocks away, not to mention, I got engaged one street over! Oak Street is one of the most well-known shopping streets in the city–it has the cream of the crop of luxury shops, but also lot’s of great everyday brands, restaurants, and salons, too! They’ve got something for everybody, and this time of year, it’s extra magical! Window shopping on and around Oak Street with a cup of hot cocoa is a winter activity that really can’t be beat! Here are some of my favorite spots to shop, eat, and stay on and around Oak Street! I hadn’t been into Kate Spade in ages, as I’ve moved further and further west as the years have gone on! They have so many adorable winter items–one of my favorites being this black and white striped scarf with POCKETS! (YASSS.) You know me–I can never get enough stripes, so layering it over a striped tee was really a no-brainer. I love how thick and structured this version is, which makes it the perfect tee for winter! Also, can we talk about these shoes!? I squealed a little when I saw them on the shelf! They’re the perfect holiday shoe and they make any outfit so much fun. (Even, ahem, a t-shirt and jeans.) Vince makes the most magical sweaters, so popping in here (especially in the cold!) is always a no-brainer. They have a lot of great classic staples that are amazing quality. A store I can never resist popping into whenever I pass by! This summer they also added a monograming station. They do it on the spot, which is so much fun to watch! (This is also where I got my favorite ever Transport tote, which you can see styled here!) Perusing Barney’s and ending at the top floor at their restaurant, Fred’s, is always such a fun weekend activity. Stop in for lunch, dinner, or a cocktail. The vibe is very fun and swanky–it makes me feel like a fancy lady who lunches ;-P One of my favorite restaurants in Chicago! Neal and I went on an impromptu date here when we first started dating and I have the best memories of our experience here. It’s Vietnamese-French fusion and is so delicious. The vibe is dark and romantic–I can’t think of a better date spot. (P.S. speaking of dates–here are 36 questions to ask on your next one.) I love love the Public Hotel. If you’re visiting Chicago, you must stay here! Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog January 21, 2019   Hii guys!  How was your weekend?! I hope you had a great one (and that you get the holiday off today in celebration of Dr. Martin Luther King and all he accomplished for our country ). So, the one thing I’ve been hearing across the board from my reader survey, especially when it comes to winter, is that we are all SOOO sick of wearing the same things over and over! (For those of us in Chicago…we have a full 2-3 months left of it ?) so you’re really looking for tips on how to re-wear what you already own.  Several of you also asked me if it’s acceptable to wear white jeans in the winter–GREAT question. (That old “no white after Labor Day” old wives tale still haunts us, doesn’t it?) And, while this is, of course, a matter of opinion, as ALL “style rules” are–I say GO FOR IT. (I hate style rules. Those are dumb–wear what makes you happy!)  Also, shout out to my favorite hotel (and bar, and restaurant!) The Robey for letting us shoot on your balcony! (If you want to stalk more of their beautiful cafe, see this post from last year!)  So, today, that is exactly what we’re diving into… Before we get into my three winter white jeans outfits below, I thought it would be helpful to share a couple tips. (I don’t like to say “do’s and don’ts” because I think you should do whatever you please) but, you know–a few guidelines are always helpful. Here are some things to keep in mind:  My reasoning for this is because this is probably the most foolproof way to still maintain a “winter” feel to your outfits. You’ll see here that I clearly went with a camel/white/cream/tan color scheme. I love this because it not only looks incredibly chic, but if you’re really worried about appearing too “springy”–that’s virtually impossible. NOBODY wears camel in the spring or summer. It is strictly a fall/winter color! ? I also love white pants in the winter paired with red and navy–or even a pretty burgundy or emerald. I think as long as you avoid really summery or springy colors, you don’t run the risk of looking out of place!  While white pants may not be intuitively “winter” to you–when you’re wearing seasonally appropriate shoes with them, it’s pretty easy to make it feel wintery. You can’t wear boots (or any closed toed shoes for that matter) in the summer, can you? Of course not–so don’t overthink it TOO much!  I think it’s easy to forget just how versatile a pair of white jeans and a classic turtleneck are, so I wanted to keep the same top and bottom to show you three very different ways to style with mixing and matching just accessories.  The white jeans you see here are from Madewell. They are the only pair of white skinny jeans that I own, and I really love them. I was on a white jean hunt for quite awhile, so I asked you guys what your favorite pairs were, and Madewell’s High Rise White Skinnies were the most popular–so I gave them a try! They do not disappoint–not even REMOTELY see through (I was wearing black underwear here, for reference, if you didn’t believe me! ?) They are high rise but not TOO high (they don’t come above my belly button–they’re a 9″ rise, for reference–so they’re SLIGHTLY higher than mid rise) and they run true to size. Shopbop also sells a lot of Madewell jeans (but when you buy them at Shopbop you get Amazon Prime shipping!)  They’re also a great amount of stretch (but they don’t bag out) and are quite comfortable! Come in Regular, Petite, Tall and Extra Tall!  And if you need ’em super fast, order them from Shopbop! (They have Amazon Prime shipping!)   I LOVE a great camel sweater. In particular, a turtleneck–but you could easily use any sweater of your choosing for any of these outfits. Mine is from Lord and Taylor (the best price you can find for cashmere!) and is sold out in this color, but you guys always rave about J.Crew’s cashmere sweaters (basically Identical to what I’m wearing here. I don’t own any personally, but have been told by a few people to size up!). Also, I love Everlane’s cashmere too (a bit softer than L&T’s but then again it’s more expensive, granted, still a great price at $120–so it’s up to you which is more important to you! I have their $100 cashmere crew in “frost donegal”  that I LOVE! You can see it styled here!)  P.S. my turtleneck collar is totally messed up in all these photos and I didn’t notice until I edited them. Def not trying to make a fashion statement. Oh well! ?C’est la vie.     This look is perfect for a variety occasions–it would be super cute for brunch or even dinner! I love that it feels crisp and classic, but the mules give it an on-trend, more minimalistic-chic twist!  Speaking of these white mules, I fell in LOVE with these white mules from Madewell (TTS) this fall, and the fact that they are closed toed and also not stark white makes them very wearable for winter as well. They also sell a lot of other Madewell items at  Shopbop–which is great because PRIME SHIPPING! Some people seem to wonder if white shoes are “okay” to wear–but I think the whole “white shoes aside from sneakers are a faux-pas” thing stems from our mothers’ generation–(I think they got burned by the white shoe craze of the 60’s and 70’s ?) but I think they make your outfit look really fresh–and I am here for them all year round!  I also wanted to include an outfit with my trench coat, because so many of you don’t live in sub-zero climates and have been asking for my suggestions on trenches/rain coats. I absolutely LOVE THIS COAT which is made by London Fog. They have a ton of similar styles though, so if you don’t see your size in my exact coat, don’t worry–there are plenty of others to choose from (like this one and this one) that the brand makes as well! You can shop them all right here!     Another look that is super versatile and could work for pretty much any occasion–especially when you work in a casual semi–casual environment, but may have a client meeting that day! I love a good blazer, especially a tweed one. This one is from Everlane and runs true to size, but any great blazer will work here (whether it’s fitted, or oversized–I love their oversized blazer too!)–I think a blazer puts the perfect amount of polish on any outfit, and the white jeans make it feel a bit more “easy”–if you know what I mean. Nordstrom has a lot of cute blazers, too!  I kept with the neutral theme and styled two of these looks with Everlane’s Modern Loafer, which I would highly recommend. They need breaking in for sure, but they are beautiful and make every outfit feel refined and modern at the same time. Go up 1/2 size! If you want more classic looking loafers, I highly recommend Sam Edelman’s loafers–I own them in leopard print (but they come in tons of colors) and they are insanely comfortable–no break in required!  The prettiest, most polished tote that is perfect for the office! If you’re looking for more tote bag reccos, I love the Madewell Transport Tote and own it in two colors! It’s easy to forget the option of layering a sweater on a sweater–but it can result in a really cute and interesting look! I especially love the look of a turtleneck and a cardigan mixed together–they are different enough that it just works–but you have to make sure they’re different textures–it works best if the cardigan is the chunkier knit!  This cardigan is from Evereve–it’s SO incredibly soft and cozy. Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog September 20, 2018  Happy Thursday, guys!  Bumping up this post from the archives this morning as scarf season is upon us and I’ve been getting quite a few questions on how I tie my scarves–so, here we go!   It’s no secret that I have a major thing for French style. French women always seem so impeccably chic and stylish without ever trying too hard. I think they’re the true definition of “perfectly undone.”  Truth be told, I think gathering inspiration from french style has made me a more confident dresser. It’s not rooted in trends or brands or labels–it emphasizes classic silhouettes, never aiming for perfection but instead, embracing and finding beauty in the imperfections. French style has taught me that you can make a statement with a simple outfit and a bold red lip, or focus on finding a few perfect wardrobe staples and wearing them for everything–to work, to out on a date, and on the weekend, too.  One Parisian style staple is the classic scarf. Whenever I need to add a little something to my outfit, I usually pull out my favorite silk scarf or bandana–it truly makes even the most basic outfit to the next level. This has actually been one of my most requested tutorials, so I’m so excited to share the two main ways I typically tie mine! Note: scarves all very in size, but you’ll want to make sure you have a SQUARE scarf. The dimensions aren’t that important–the method is still the same–but for reference, the one I use here is 36″ x 36.”  This is the most classic “french girl” way to wear a scarf. It’s so easy, and if you have a shorter scarf, you can skip the middle steps (wrapping it around your neck twice)–simply roll it diagonally and tie it in a knot!  Step one: First, you’ll want to begin with a square-ish scarf, folded it in half diagonally to form a triangle. It can be a big square or a little square, but typically this is the shape of scarf that works best for these particular tying methods. I’ve found that typically the vintage scarves I found are larger like the one I’m using here–but a lot of the one’s you see sold new are more “bandana” size. (You can see my how to tie a bandana tutorial here.) Regardless, the method is the same!  Step two: Begin rolling from the long edge (hotdog style, if you will, remember that from grade school? Haha!) to the corner until you have it rolled into a nice little “rope” if you will.  Step three: Then, wrap scarf around your neck once (kind of like you would with a regular scarf!) You should then have two loose ends.  Step four: Tie those ends together. (Depending on the material of your scarf, it might stay fine like this, or you may need to knot it.) To finish, I like to move the knot to the side so it’s a bit off-center.  You’re done!   Good news, this method is nearly identical to the one outlined above! Nearly the same steps, but a totally different look!  Step one: Fold your square scarf in half diagonally.  Step two: The beginning of this step will vary based on how large you want the “triangle” part of your bandana to be. If you have an average size square scarf, you can simply move on to step three. Or, if you have a larger scarf (or you just want your bandana to be smaller) you can roll the edge a bit like we did before–begin rolling the scarf starting with the longest edge, toward the end. Unlike we did above, don’t roll the scarf all the way to the corner–stop halfway through (where you stop will dictate how large the “bandana” portion is.) You will now have a long rectangular roll with a little triangle on the end.  Holding the triangular portion (it should resemble a bandana type shape at this point, like a bandit, haha!) in front of your body, and wrap the ends around your neck once. (Just like the motions above, this time, it’s just a different shape!)  Step three: Like we did in the first tutorial, tie the ends together. Leave them hanging after one tie, or you can tie into a knot for more security. Depending on your preference, you can tie the ends OVER the bandana (triangle), or UNDER the it. Leave them hanging out, or you can tuck the loose ends underneath the triangular portion of the bandana for a cleaner look. There’s no wrong way to do it–I think it just depends on what you’re going for, and also, how much of your scarf you’d like to show off!  I like to finish by twisting the scarf so it’s a bit off to the side–I prefer mine not to be centered, but again, it’s really up to you!  Super easy, right? I’m pretty confident that a scarf like this looks good with almost anything, but if you’re looking for inspiration, here are a few notable “French style” looks I’ve worn with scarves:  If you missed this post on my “wear anywhere outfit” from last year, the outfit you see above is my #1 go-to outfit in the fall, winter and spring. It works for nearly every occasion–it’s cute, but polished, fashionable-yet professional. The scarf is definitely the cherry on top! My exact trench is restocked this year, as is my favorite Everlane silk button down. My jeans are very old, but if you’re looking for new skinnies I highly recommend Everlane’s new stretch skinny jeans that come in medium or high rise. Similar booties here!  Pair a t-shirt dress (I love this one and it’s quickly become a cult classic that everyone is talking about! I love the sleeveless version as well! For both, size up if you want a looser fit!) with a leather jacket and white sneakers. The scarf brings everything together and adds some polish to a sportier outfit.  Stripes are a french outfit staple for good reason–they look so cute with everything! I love pairing red with stripes in particular, so this red bandana gets plenty of use! My striped tee is old but there are lot’s of similar versions here! I love wearing this outfit with shorts in the summer and classic Levi’s in the winter! (P.S. I have a separate how to tie a bandana tutorial if you’re curious!)   I wore several variations of this outfit in Paris (full post here!) I love pairing a scarf with a button down (mine is old, but similar here!) and high-waisted jeans!   Red, white, blue, and camel are one of my favorite color combinations in the fall and winter! The silk scarf really puts the outfit over the top and adds a needed dash of pattern! (This outfit is super old, but you can see the new camel coat I just purchased here, similar loafers, similar sweater, and my favorite white jeans!)  Where to buy square scarves and bandanas:  Admittedly, sometimes I think the best scarves come from the $5 scarf bin in your favorite vintage store! However, there are a lot of cute new ones out right now too, if vintage isn’t your thing! The one I’m wearing here is Hermes. Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog May 3, 2018   Denim shirt: J.Crew–available at Nordstrom as well as J.Crew. If you’re looking for one that’s a little bit more oversized or longer, I love this relaxed boyfriend/long chambray shirt. I also love this Abercrombie version and this version that ties in the front–so cute! Jeans: Levi’s Wedgie Straight Jeans–they come in SO many different colors and washes and are available a bunch of places–Nordstrom and Shopbop have a great selection. Navy slides: J.Crew Factory (on sale for $83! Also come in pink and black!) I also love these twist block-heeled mules if you prefer an open toe for spring! Neck scarf: J.Crew (sold out) but similar here and love this cute pink one, too! Bag: Madewell Transport Tote (my favorite tote ever. Fits so much stuff and also comes in so many pretty colors!) Beret: Urban Outfitters (they have the best berets–I’ve also bought ones off of Amazon that were too big and floppy and looked awful ? save yourself the hassle and just buy this one!!) Sunnies: Ray Ban Lipstick: RMS beauty’s “RMS red” Hair & Makeup: See my everyday makeup tutorial here and my everyday hair tutorial here! I’m Louisville bound today, guys! (SF —> Kentucky Derby! Boy am I gunna be TIRED on Sunday or what? ?) As I’m writing this, I realize I actually just wore this exact outfit in San Francisco, just paired with my trusty white sneaks. I told you–serial outfit repeater, I am! Side note, I recently added a new addition to my already denim-heavy wardrobe–this J.Crew jean jacket. Now we’ve got a real Canadian Tuxedo infestation over here. (Can you tell that denim is a fashion trend I am 110% behind? Does denim even count as a trend? I don’t think so ? when has denim ever NOT been in style?) Anyway, if you’re a denim lover like me, I hope you’re excited for today’s post–we’re talking all about how to style one of my favorite staples–the Chambray shirt! (Side note–we shot this in the Waldorf Astoria Courtyard in the VERY spot that Neal proposed. Awwwww. All the feels. See those photos and read how he popped the question in this post!)     I have always been a huge fan of denim on denim. I know sometimes it can be a daunting thing to try out, but it’s easier to pull off than you might think! My only tip would be to avoid pairing dark denim with dark denim–you may start to feel like Mario or Luigi then–but otherwise, you should be good ? (Remember that joke? DENIM DENIM DENIM.) Another tip–mix in some feminine elements with your denim on denim outfit, because without something to juxtapose your Canadian Tuxedo, you may start to feel a little bit costumey–(or not, of course, this is totally based on your personal style and preference!) For example, here I’ve mixed in some more girly pieces–the blush beret and navy mules–along with some classic elements–the neck scarf and red lip. These little tricks transform what would’ve felt like a very “tomboyish” outfit into a polished one that is polished while still being casual and on-trend.   If the Canadian Tuxedo thing is too much for you, wearing your denim shirt or jacket (this is the one I’m wearing above and I love it so much!!) with white jeans (mine are the kick-crop jeans from Everlane! They stretch out quite a bit so if you’re in between, go with the smaller size!) is a much easier way to ease into the denim on denim trend! The espadrille platforms also add–(see? this trick again!) a more feminine element to keep the outfit fresh and springy along with my silk peplum tank! (How cute would this summer outfit be with a white denim skirt, too! This one is so cute and only $49!)  Don’t feel like throwing on a jean jacket? A denim shirt is a really cute alternative (especially if the weather is too heavy for a jean jacket, but there’s still a slight chill in the air!) Tying one around your waist is also a really cute way to tone down a feminine dress like the one above and make it feel less girly. (Side note, these shoes–Everlane’s “Day Heels”– are probably my favorite year-round staples in my wardrobe! Come in tons of colors and are SO comfortable! You can walk in them for miles! If you’re in between sizes go with the larger size!) This is another one of my favorite spring/ summer outfits! One of the comfiest outfits in the world? Pairing your chambray shirt with leggings! I do this a lot when I travel–if you don’t like your bum to be uncovered while in leggings (ah, the old “leggings aren’t real pants” debacle!)–opt for a long denim shirt, boyfriend style. This look is especially cute paired with Allbirds or my favorite Jack Purcell white sneakers and a cute bandana or neck scarf! P.S. These are the leggings you guys are always raving about! I need to try them!  Again, if the whole monochromatic denim thing isn’t working for you, try contrasting colors instead. Go for a skinny jean in either black (an easy way to dress up your denim shirt!) or dark blue paired with a light blue denim shirt and you’ll feel less “chic auto mechanic.” (The jeans I’m wearing above are VERY old from Madewell, but this Abercrombie pair is really similar–and I’m obsessed with their jeans! They are so similar to Madewell’s!) This looks especially cute with a lighter colored jacket–like a white linen blazer like mine above (to make it more professional or polished) or a light colored suede jacket! Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog October 20, 2017   **Click PLAY to watch the video** Happy Friday! We’re back with another Capsule Wardrobe Remix post–hooray! I’m really excited about today’s post! Not only is this t-shirt dress one of my very favorite wardrobe staples, but I think the concept here can really revolutionize how you look at your wardrobe–this will also come in especially handy when it comes to packing for a trip! (Side note: If you haven’t read this post, go do that first, then come back here and read this! I want to make sure you’re all caught up to speed on our new series!) Today’s concept: One dress, four ways, from work to weekend. So, you know the drill! Before we get into the looks, let’s go through the handful of items we need to create these looks: Black t-shirt dress: I kind of think this was the unsung hero of this month’s capsule–you’ll see why, but I am in LOVE with this black t-shirt dress.  I wear it ev-er-y-where. It’s great on the plane, out to dinner, to the office, on a date–later on, I even show you a sneaky hidden belt trick to make it shorter when you want to go out on the town ? There’s also a similar one at H&M! This one and this one are also good ones! Heeled Booties: These booties by 1.State go with everything I own, they are SO comfy, and are only $99! I love the shape of the toe and the fact that they’re cut out in the back too, which adds a little more visual interest! Because of the shape and color, they also help to elongate your leg, which is hard to find in a bootie, as most of the time they can cut you off at the ankles and make your legs look stubby! (You also saw them worn in my outfit post earlier this week!) I also just got these booties from Bloomingdales that I’m obsessed with if you’re looking for a more classic style. Leather tote: The Madewell Transport tote making the capsule wardrobe cut comes as a shock to absolutely none of you, I am sure. It’s my everything bag. Work, travel, groceries–whatever, this is always the bag I’m reaching for and it comes in several styles and colors as well. Black pumps: I’ve owned this particular pair of Sam Edelman pumps for years. They’re slingbacks, and they’ve since been discontinued, but this pair is super similar in the d’Orsay style. This ankle strap version is adorable, too! I love Sam Edelman shoes (Nordstrom has a good selection and Shopbop’s selection is also diverse and totally different) They’re one of my go-to brands for footwear. Black OTK boots: I own two pairs of black OTK boots. In this month’s series, I’ll be styling the Stuart Weitzman Lowlands, but I always refer people to the Blondo Olivia’s, which I also own and love, if they want something more budget-friendly. The Blondo version are waterproof, which is AMAZING in the winter. You never have to worry about saving your precious suede boots from the weather, and they are stretchy in the back, which means they are the only budget-friendly pair I’ve found that fit my tiny child calves, but also stretch to fit all calf sizes, too! Trench coat: I purchased this trench by London Fog last Spring before my trip to London and it is one of my very favorite coats for both Fall and Spring. It has a detachable hood as well as a removable liner. Which unlike a lot of coats, does add a significant amount of warmth. I absolutely adore it and it’s one of my favorite jackets. It looks super chic for work, and just as pretty for dinner or a stroll around the neighborhood. Leather jacket: I now own two leather jackets–one brown and one black. The black one is my newest addition and I don’t know what took me so long to get one! I definitely love both colors and I think whichever color is best for you just depends on your preferences. The one I feature this month is sadly sold out but this one from Bernardo is similar. Bernardo makes a ton of really quality leather jackets that always get rave reviews. This one from BlankNYC is also super cute and under $100! (I’ll also be linking more options down below). Leopard clutch: For the same reasons as I sing the praises of the leopard loafer, I love this leopard clutch. (Nordstrom actually has a TON of different leopard clutches right now!) I’m a huge fan of it for going out because it brightens up even the most basic outfit. Plus, it’s such a steal for less than $50 and it looks and feels like the designer version. Crossbody: I was so on the fence when I purchased this crossbody (it’s Rebecca Minkoff’s ‘Love’ bag in size small!) as to whether or not I would wear it, but I’d have to say it’ snow become one of my most reached for bags. I really love the fact that it’s olive, which is a neutral, but a really fun mix-up from the typical tan or grey. Although my exact version in the olive color is no longer available in the smaller size, this one is nearly identical, just slightly larger! I also like the Mini “Mac” bag in olive suede as well! Neck scarf: Another one that won’t shock you a bit ? I’m a huge fan of the dainty neck scarf (I love this one from J.Crew!) and I think it’s the perfect accessory to add a little French inspiration to your outfit. I own over a dozen! eBay is a great place to get vintage ones, too! Belts: My gold buckle belt is Topshop and has since sold out (boo!) but this one is really similar and so is this one! I also have a cool trick I’ll show you later on in the post that requires a skinny belt (I have a skinny leopard belt like this one that’s really cute, but any skinny belt will do–it won’t be visible!) Ready to do it? Let’s go! The true test of any wardrobe staple–does it pass the “office” test? This black t-shirt dress definitely does. Now, of course, everyone’s office dress code is different, so feel free to improvise as you need, but for the most part, I think this number would be deemed appropriate in most work settings! (Not to mention, it’s so soft, it feels like pajamas.) Many t-shirt dresses don’t have much shape to them, so it’s most flattering if you use a belt (mine is old, this one is similar) to emphasize your waist! Pair with classic black pumps and your office tote, throw on your trench, and you’re ready to go. Also worth noting–you can never go wrong with top knot. Your boss thinks it looks polished–only you know that it’s disguising your two day old mop. (This is how I do my top knot!)  [/one-half]  Alright. Well, this was easy. Swap the pumps for booties, your work bag for a cute leopard clutch (I love this one, too!), and swipe on some deep red lipstick (I’ve been loving Lilah B.’s dual purpose lip & cheek color in “B.Memorable” that I’m wearing here!) and you’re good to go! I wear this look out on Friday night when Neal and I are roaming around the neighborhood! These booties are the perfect “going out” height for when you’ll be doing a fair amount of walking and need something comfortable, but want something that looks cute too! (For those who are interested, this is how I curl my hair!)     You guys KNOW I was secretly supposed to be born a French girl, so I’m all about the neck scarf. I think it’s one of the easiest ways to take your look from boring to super chic. If you’re unsure which colors to get, don’t overthink it! I’d recommend going with a dark navy, white, and red mix because those colors pair well with everything. The colors in the scarf you see here are navy–often when you wear navy with black, the navy either looks black, or provides a nice contrast. I’m very into mixing black and navy! Anyway, for this look, I also came up with a sneaky little belt trick for when you want to shorten your hemline in a snap: belt a skinny belt around your dress, and then pull it out so the fabric falls over the belt. It defines your waist, shortens the dress, and you can barely tell the belt is there to begin with! (See the demo in the video at the top of this post!) This is definitely how you can get the most wear out of your casual dresses from the office to date night. I opted for a crossbody because it’s perfect for both day and night and still roomy enough to fit all of your essentials! The olive color ensures it’s a neutral that goes with absolutely everything, and the suede material adds a little something extra to your outfit!     Remember that skinny belt trick I showed you to shorten your dress? You also see that here! There are few style combinations I love more than a short dress with OTK boots–it makes your legs look miles long! (Here I’m wearing the Stuart Weitzman Lowlands, but I always refer people to the Blondo Olivia’s, which I also own and love, if they want something more budget-friendly. They’re also waterproof AND on sale right now!!) To top off the look, pull on a leather jacket (this one is similar to mine and on sale!), grab that fun patterned clutch, and you’ve got the perfect outfit for Saturday night!      Also, make sure to subscribe over on my Youtube Channel so you’ll be the first to know when I upload a new video! Make sure to check out October’s Capsule Wardrobe Reveal, How to Wear Leather Leggings Three Ways, and my favorite capsule travel outfits.
