Last week on IG stories (per usual) I asked for SO much feedback regarding alllll kinds of topics here on the blog, and the topic of “basics” really kept popping up in particular, so, I thought, for this month’s post in partnership with Everlane (we’ve got one more slated for October too! ) it would be a great time to focus on just that–simple pieces you can wear tons of different ways!  Or, as my idol, Ina Garten would call it, “Back to Basics!”  Whenever someone asks for my suggestions on wardrobe staples and basics, my first responses is almost always “EVERLANE!” They truly make the best quality staples for the best prices. They have their own [ethical!] factories (which you can read all about here!) and they sell direct to you and me–the consumers, without the crazy markup! They’re all about transparency, from knowing exactly where your clothes are made, to how much profit margin they make on each item! (Scroll down on each product page and it will list how much every stage of the production process costs in relation to how much they sell the item for! It’s really cool!)  So–now that you have my stamp of approval that all these basics I’m about to show you are 100% Jess approved…shall we jump in?  Let’s start with the essential items in this capsule. (You’ll notice many of them are *not* strictly fall items, but evergreen items you’ll wear year-round! Hopefully this gives you some great ideas of how to style any items you currently have, and gives you some good reccos if you’ve been wanting to upgrade! )   This blouse was SUCH a hit in my capsule wardrobe from last month (I wore it here in white) that I decided to order it in black to see if it lived up to the hype! I’ve been wanting a black blouse for awhile now and you guys will be VERY happy to learn that this one is not remotely see through (I know that’s a big concern of everyone’s!) It’s also washable! I love how soft it is (its almost a velvety texture) and it’s really more of a charcoal than a black! It’s perfect for work, and for a date night, you can unbutton one button (or even wear a lacy bralette or something underneath if you want!)      I love a good cotton tee, and Everlane’s are my personal favorite of them all! Personally, I just love this classic, super soft crewneck tee. What I do is I always either tuck mine in or knot them, and this one is easy to style both ways! I love a white tee because you can dress it up or dress it down and it always looks simple but chic. It’s also not remotely see through! (Tip: If you keep finding that all white shirts are see through, you’re probably wearing the wrong color nude bra–it needs to match your skin tone!) Sizing: Runs TTS, wearing a small.   I’ve had these jeans many seasons now and they are one of my favorites in particular for fall. I love the medium wash on them that looks classic and really nice with everything! I always say that if you’ve been wanting to get out of a skinny jean rut and try something new–but that the whole straight leg/wide leg thing feels too much for you––these will be your jeans! I wear size 25, and I’m 5’6 for height reference.   If you love the look of a sleek, classic pump but aren’t a big fan of heels, you will love these. The heels are very low and manageable, and I adore the square detail that shoes the perfect amount of toe cleavage. These are perfect for everything from work to date nights. Sizing: Run TTS   Blazers are always such a popular layer for fall. Everlane’s version is super well-made, flattering, and the perfect balance of trendy and polished. Sizing: Supposed to be oversized, but I’d say if you’re on the cusp, go down a size. (I.E. This one is super easy to dress up or down!  Sizing: I’m wearing a 0, so I’d say this runs true to size. It’s a-line and short, but not TOO short. (It passes the old fingertip trick ) making it suitable for many office environments as well!   You guys know I’m a sucker for a great trench coat, and this is SUCH a classic, adorable twist. Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog January 16, 2018   So, you’ve been looking for a pair of pants that you can wear to work and on the weekends? To a board meeting or on an airplane? With heels or with sneakers? Conservative enough for church but sexy enough for a night out? (It’s like we have ESPN or something…) These magic pants exist. They’re called ponte pants. If you don’t know, now you know. I figured they were the best way to break the extremely long accidental hiatus I took from the Capsule Wardrobe Remix series over the holidays. (SORRY! I swear I blinked in November and it became January!) But I’m excited to say, IT’S BACK! (Make sure you see the full list of items in my Winter Capsule wardrobe in this post!) Anyway, I also heard you loud and clear on your request for more office-appropriate outfits, so, no matter what the dress code is at your 9-5, I can assure you, you’ll be reaching for these pants several times over throughout the work-week, as well as outside of work, too! The pair I’m styling here is made by Halogen, which is one of my favorite brands for basic wardrobe staples–they also come in charcoal grey, which would be great for work as well. Nordstrom has a huge selection of ponte pants, too. If you’re wanting ones that are less tapered (i.e. look more like work slacks) Madewell makes a version that you may like! Read on for four ways to style ’em! Are you sick of my silk Everlane button down yet? ? Hopefully not, because this won’t be the last time you see it! It’s probably my #1 most worn item of my entire wardrobe, and for good reason. It really is one of the most versatile things you can own. It’s a match made in heaven for ponte pants and some chic black pumps. To mix things up, I unbuttoned a few buttons from the bottom of the shirt and tied it up, which is a new alternative to the front tuck, which defines your waist and elongates your legs! (Shirt sizing tip: Runs TTS but is supposed to be a relaxed fit. If you want it tighter you can go a size down! I’m wearing a size 2 here.)      I always find myself constantly rushing, so if you’re the same, this is another reason you’ll love these pants. Anything that minimizes rushing is a win in my book. These pants essentially eliminate the need to go home and change for your movie date after work. Just bring another top and a change of shoes and do the desk-side switcheroo. Told you–these pants go with everything! Here I paired them with my favorite tall boots (they have a low, chunky heel, which is great because I think the heel makes them easier to dress up, but still really comfortable! Run TTS!) and a classic black turtleneck. (Mine is old but this one is very similar and a great price–reviews say to size down! Everlane also makes a really pretty one!) Also, my black Barbour Beadnell!        When I put on this outfit, Cassandra stopped mid-sentence and stared at me for a good 5 seconds before blurting out, “oh my god, that is the cutest outfit I have ever seen.” Some of the best outfits catch you by surprise–but almost all of them have one thing in common–they’re simple, but significant–to steal the words of Don Draper. I think that’s going to be my motto when getting dressed this year. What you didn’t notice at first, is that the foundation of this outfit is actually outfit #1: ponte pants, my silk button down (untied) with my favorite camel crewneck layered over it. (My sweater is old, but similar here, here, and here!) I paired it with my favorite oxfords (which I also love in black!), but this look would also be really cute with loafers. (Neal got me the Gucci loafers for Christmas and they are UNREAL and so comfortable, but I also own the Sam Edelman ones (I have the leopard but they come in tons of colors and are also amazing and super comfy!)      Alright, I broke the technical capsule rules here because I subbed out the striped turtleneck from the original list for this striped tee. #1, because I can’t find a dupe of the white striped turtleneck with black stripes anywhere anymore, and #2–you REALLY, REALLY need to know about this tee. It’s REVERSIBLE! One side is boatneck, the other is v-neck. How amazing is that? (Awesome for travel, too! It’s basically 2 shirts in one!) Plus, it’s insanely soft. I feel like this might be one of the first outfits to come to mind when you hear the phrase, “Jess Keys outfit.” It’s got all my favorite staples: stripes, neck scarf, Barbour jacket, tall boots. I really like the juxtaposition of the feminine details of the shirt and scarf paired with the more masculine Barbour coat–contrasts like this always make for the most foolproof outfits. Also come in grey!), Gucci Loafers (Similar version on sale!)   Happy Saturday everybody! Apologies for the SEVERE delay in getting my Friday post up–typically I only post Monday through Friday but I actually had such a great conversation with you guys over on Instagram that I decided to switch up the direction of what I had originally planned. Here’s why: Everyone and their mom is posting about the Nordstrom sale. I’m so sick of it already and I’m a BLOGGER. I love that colorful striped Topshop sweater and in all honestly, I wanted to buy it SO BAD but if I see it in my instagram feed one more time I might scream. That being said, I KNOW you guys want to see my coverage of the sale because you told me so! I don’t want to not cover it because it’s an AMAAZZINGGGG sale. So, what I decided to do is frankly have a conversation with you guys on Instagram about how I could make my sale coverage MORE helpful–the answer? A resounding “please please please more staples that work for work and the weekend!!” I’m SO glad I asked you–this is something I wouldn’t have thought of! Turns out, based on my polls, you guys are looking for mostly tops, dresses, and layering pieces–so, THAT is what I am giving you today! Remember, the Nordstrom sale is full of FALL pieces, so I won’t be showing any summery staples here. Every single item used in these collages is part of the sale, too! Huzzah! (Side note I kind of rushed through these collages, they are not my best work, but luckily I know you’ll forgive me because the outfits are good, I promise ?) Let’s jump in, yeah!? When is the office NOT an arctic tundra, am I right? This is why layering pieces are key. Here, I picked a blazer to highlight for our looks because it’s extremely versatile, polished, and perfect for in AND out of the office. Most importantly, a lot of you told me you struggle with how to style a blazer, so hopefully this gives you four great ideas! Also, you could easily swap out the blazer for a cardigan here, and the looks would be just as cute! Why I chose THIS particular blazer: I really like this one because it’s tailored, but not TOO tailored. It also doesn’t feel like a suit or tuxedo jacket, it toes the line between classic and on-trend, yet polished. It also comes in four colors–black, white, and blush. (Several of you told me you were in search of a good white blazer, and this is a great one!) It’s a great price at $64!  There are also a lot of trendier blazers right now (like this one, SO cute!) that tend to be more boxy–those are super cute, but they aren’t as flattering on all body types, so just be mindful of that. My blazer styling trick: I am an avid sleeve roller. If my sleeves aren’t rolled on my blazer, I feel like I’m wearing a costume, but with the sleeves rolled, it’s just the right amount of effortless perfect imperfection! Also, if you feel like your blazer doesn’t look quite right, roll the sleeves, and you’ll probably love it! If you want a comfier blazer you can move in: This Caslon knit blazer for $39 and this more relaxed knit longline blazer for $65 are awesome and similar to the J.Crew sweater blazer that was super popular last year–remember that one? They’re knit so you can move around in it a lot easier and have the comfort of something that feels more like a sweater, with a little more polish. (Teachers, these are especially perfect for you!) Shop more favorite on-sale blazers and layering pieces:   Okay, so you’ve got your ideal blazer or layering piece picked out, here’s how to style it!  1901 Cropped Pants: I absolutely LOVE these pants made by 1901–which is one of Nordstrom’s own brands! (I think they’re new, I’ve never noticed them before!) The brand makes timeless pieces with a modern twist, and I think it might be one of my favorite new brands ever! Anyway, these cropped pants are totally on-trend while being completely polished enough for the office (which as you know, isn’t an easy feat!) Striped tee: You rarely think about being able to dress up t-shirts, but it’s so easy to do as long as you have the RIGHT shirt. This one, again, is 1901 brand and is very polished–even if you work in a strict business casual environment, it’s completely appropriate under a blazer! Adding a pop of pattern adds so much interest to the outfit! Leopard mules: Speaking of pattern, my favorite two pattern combinations are stripes and leopard. They are the perfect opposites and are a failsafe combination to make any outfit interesting–I’m especially a huge fan of leopard shoes for the office, because often workwear can get SO boring and they go a long way to spice up anything bland. Classic tote: I don’t own a Kate Spade tote myself, but when I did my “Real Women Approved: The Best Tote Bags for Work and Travel” roundup, you guys RAVED about Kate Spade’s totes! I noticed this one is part of the sale and it’s really pretty and comes in three versatile colors–it’s 13″ so it’s big enough to fit a small laptop, too! See what I did there? I took the same blazer, tee, and shoes and swapped them out for this adorable button-down camel skirt and neckscarf. BOOM! Totally different look, but just as fashionable, and just as polished! (This is such a Jackie-O look–well, except she probably would’ve subbed Gucci Loafers ?).  Okay, so, it appears that this is where a lot of you struggle–styling a blazer OUT of the office. You love ’em, they’re easy to wear for work, but how the heck do you wear them outside of the office without feeling like you’re trying too hard? First, remember the sleeve rolling trick. Then, do go with combinations like these: Denim skirt: I chose a black version here, but you can use any version you like! It would look super cute with a white denim skirt for early fall, or a blue denim skirt, too! The great part about a denim skirt is that it’s a bit more edgy with the raw hem–you always want to play with juxtaposition when you’re putting outfits together, so if you start with something preppy, like a blazer, it works well to pair it with something that is the OPPOSITE of preppy–in this instance, it’s “edgy.” (I mean, just a little bit of edge though. You know how “edgy” I am ?) Striped tee: You know what I say, everything is cuter with stripes ? I also love the v-neck of this tee, as they tend to be more flattering than crew-necks. (Note: this is especially true if you have a larger bust!) The stripes bring a necessary element of personality to the outfit. There’s a long sleeve crewneck version as well, if that’s more your speed. Classic White Sneakers: I haven’t seen these before–these are the “shoreline” with rose gold rivets! Cute neck scarf: Few outfits don’t look cuter with a neck scarf. French girl graphic tee: While a blazer can be business-like, a graphic tee is fun and playful and brings a fun little twist to the outfit! Cute booties: Of course, the pillar of the fall wardrobe–the bootie! If you missed my raving in my previous post–these are made by a shoe brand I can’t recommend enough–Blondo. When we booked our trip to Paris months back, (it’s coming up SO SOON! Less than 3 weeks!) I started having visions of Neal and I strolling through the city with no particular plan in mind, picnicking on the Seine, eating baguettes, and me wearing some incredibly french-inspired outfits of breezy button white downs, stripes, scarves, bare-faced with red lipstick. Needless to say, I’m a little french-style obsessed. Here are 5 outfit hacks I’m wholeheartedly embracing during our 9 day trip to France!   French women are known for appearing “perfectly undone” because, well, they are! They don’t spend hours in the mirror doing their hair–they typically opt for au natural over a done-up ‘do. This has always been my philosophy as well–I love the look of tousled hair, which works out perfectly, because lugging a blow-drier to another country and risking a power outage fiasco does not sound like my idea of a good time. Let it down and let it air dry, or pull it back into a messy chignon–add a few pins, and you’re ready to go! I try to let my hair air dry as often as possible, and picked up a travel sized version of Bumble and Bumble’s “Don’t Blow It” air dry cream last time I got my hair cut (If you’re looking for a hair salon in Chicago–Sine Qua Non is A-MAZING!) and I’ve been loving it lately! I will definitely be stashing it in my carry-on!  In the same vein, you don’t see a lot of French girls with tons of caked on makeup, false eyelashes, and the whole shebang. A bit of foundation and some mascara are the main stays of her makeup bag–and a swipe of lipstick is enough to dress up any outfit! My two go-to red shades are M.A.C. Lady Danger and NARS Cruella! If you want a drugstore buy, I recently bought Milani’s Sweet Nectar shade–it’s an orangey-coral hue that is really great for summer!  I recently read this post on Cup of Jo and was totally inspired. She talks about how french women view their lacy bra’s as part of their outfit–a loose, white button down with a bit of black lace peeking out. I love it! Journelle has the prettiest ever lingerie, so I plan to stock up on a few pretty lacy numbers like these before we leave!  You know me–adding scarves to everything. I don’t know when I really started wearing them, but I’ve always loved the parisian-inspired look a dainty silk scarf (like this one!) creates with literally anything you pair them with! I think scarves are such a simple, but perfectly classic way to add a little punch to your outfit, and I’ve acquired quite the collection. (Oh, bandanas, too!)  French women are known for going the comfy route–jeans, flowing dresses, or donning the best ever ballet flats. I was never a huge fan of ballet flats before, but they’re really growing on me–especially the lace-up kind that are really big right now! I’m also lusting after the scalloped Chloe ballet flats, but actually found that Sam Edelman has a budget-friendly dupe! (Seriously, they look EXACTLY the same!) This classic pink pair is also perfection. I’m really considering springing for a pair of these before we head to Paris!

Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog November 1, 2018   Striped tee: old, but very similar here and here, Jeans: old but my Everlane BF jeans are similar as well as my Levi’s Wedgie Jeans! Lipstick: Beautycounter lip sheer lipstick in “coral” (I also love their color intense lipstick, if you’re looking for something brighter!) Beret: Urban Outfitters but also love Halogen’s berets! In the fall, winter, and spring, I wear a LOT of berets–they are my absolute favorite kind of hat and I think they make any outfit look SO chic, put together, and the best part–add a little bit of Parisian flair! I’m really glad berets have seen a resurgence so you can embrace them as part of your wardrobe and not feel like you’re wearing a costume ? I always get questions from you guys asking how to style them, afraid that you won’t be able to pull them off (not true!!)–so today, I’m sharing four ways to wear your beret–but truthfully, there’s no wrong way to do it, whatever makes YOU feel the most confident! First, you want to start with the right sized beret and one that is made with thick felt (cheap versions with thinner felt will look saggy and floppy–I tried ordering cheaper versions from Amazon and it did not go well ?) You also don’t want one that’s too big because then it will just look odd. Most of my berets are from Urban Outfitters but I also have one from Nordstrom that I love as well–both are the perfect size, shape, and fabric to lay correctly on your head! Rounding up my favorites below: Okay, got your favorite? Great! Here are four ways to style it:  The first is pulled straight onto your head with the beret pulled down over your forehead. This is a very common way to wear a beret and along with #2 below, is what you’ll see styled the majority of the time! If you have a longer forehead, this is likely the style that will look best on you (I prefer style #2 below, though!)  This is my favorite way to wear my beret and I typically wear it like this the majority of the time (unless it’s freezing and I just want more of my face covered, haha!) All you have to do is pull it straight on (like the above) and then pull it slightly to one side so you get that “perfectly undone” little slant look that you admire on so many French girls!    If wearing your beret forward feels a bit much for you, you can totally wear it further back on your head so it’s less “beret” like and more “beanie” like. Instead of pulling it forward over your forehead, simply only pull it on the crown of your head instead.   There’s nothing more “French girl” inspired than wearing your beret with the signature French low messy bun. This is my ultimate go-to when my hair is dirty and just overall cannot be salvaged, haha! Just twist your ponytail and secure it into a messy bun, and top with a beret (worn in style #1 or #2 always works best if your hair is up!) Shop berets:  Filed Under: Outfits, Style

Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog November 27, 2019  Happy almost Thanksgiving! I hope you get to work from home today where you’re doing that thing where you just tap your mouse every 20 minutes so it LOOKS like your “online” in your work chat OR you’re “working” from the office but really just getting a head start on your holiday shopping!? (Those were always my favorite days in the office! ) I’m so excited to be back with another Everlane post today–did you hear the news I shared on IG stories? We most recently had a three-month partnership, but it has now been extended to January! I am THRILLED! Everlane is one of my all-time favorite brands and one of my absolute favorite partners to collaborate with!  So, here we are with NOVEMBER’S post–huzzah! If you’re new here, there are so many reasons to love Everlane, and I have been a fan of theirs LONG before they ever were a blog sponsor (we’re talking like, 5+ YEARS!) but here are two big reasons why I love the company so much: 1. Transparency: They cut out the traditional retail markup and middlemen so they can sell everything at a great price, with impeccable quality. On every product page, you can scroll down to the very bottom to see how much it costs to make the item at each stage of production and in turn, how much they charge for it. 2. Ethical partners + company mission: They do a LOT more than just make great clothes–they are very focused on sustainability and have a huge goal of eliminating all virgin plastic from their supply chain by 2021! They also have a “Black Friday Fund” instead of a sale each year, where they give back to a different cause each year central to the company’s mission. By the end of this year, they will have raised over $1,000,000 for projects to improve the lives of their factory workers and clean up the environment! Anyway, this month is a little bit of a “looser” capsule than we’ve done in the past (I was quite liberal with the shoe choices in order to show a lot of variety!) but they include your top new item requests––Teddy Sweater, Alpaca Cardigan Sweater, Mockneck bodysuit, and Chelsea boots––mixed in with my other favorite Everlane staples.   Before we get into the post––I do want to point out that Everlane will not be doing discounts for Black Friday, however, this year’s Black Friday Fund helps to benefit Oceana, an organization dedicated to protecting our oceans by putting an end to single-use plastic! $10 from each order will be donated to the cause until they reach their goal of $300,000. Such an amazing cause and a great way to make a difference just by shopping! So, you don’t need to hold out for any of these items you see here to go on sale (they won’t!) however, if you’d like your dollars to help support a great cause, you can certainly wait a couple more days to purchase! Happy Friday! How are we already back to the weekend!? You know those weekends sometimes where you think you don’t have that many plans and then you look at your calendar and you’re like OH SNAP–when am I going to find time to relax!? ? Luckily there was plenty of relaxing last weekend and we have so many plans that we’re looking forward to! One of my best friends Courtney is in town from Indianapolis with her husband, mom and brand new BABY BOY! I can’t believe she’s now a mom and we can’t wait to meet baby Will! One of my other best friends, Ally (she’s the one who is from Memphis) is also coming into town to see Courtney and the baby because she happens to be at a work conference in Milwaukee–so it’s the best timing and we’ll have a big reunion and I’m really excited. Saturday night we’re also celebrating our friend Andrew’s birthday at Tuco & BlondiIe and somewhere in there we need to find time to clean out our closets before our new Container Store closets are installed next week! EEEEE! So yeah, kind of a stacked weekend. But enough about my plans–today, I’m teaching you a v. important fashion lesson.  Remember when I taught you the never-fail Juxtaposition rule of style? (If you missed it, click here to go back and read the post!) That comes into play here, because we started with a masculine piece, and then built the rest of the outfit with feminine pieces–resulting in the perfect “just right” mix. I’ve received quite a few messages from you guys asking me how to style blazers in general. I picked this one from Nordstrom because I love that it’s a longer “boyfriend” type blazer but I also think these “trendy menswear blazers” are harder to style sometimes than classic blazers, and I wanted you to get a lot out of this little post ? so I thought it would be a good example! I’m 5’6 for height/length reference–so my petite girls, this probably isn’t the best blazer for you as it will be unflatteringly long. Luckily, Nordstrom has an insane selection (which is why they are one of my favorite places to shop!) so there’s definitely something for every body type! (Anddd I especially love their “trend” section for ideas on what to wear with said blazer!) For my petite girls, I’d go with a blazer that is a little bit shorter, like this one! This one also comes in petite!) If the oversized blazer style isn’t your thing–I love this one or this one which is the same feel but a bit more fitted and classic! Nordstrom also has a lot of really cute blazers for my plus sized gals! I think sometimes blazers can feel intimidating because they are such a statement piece that can easily feel frumpy if you pair it with the wrong thing, so here’s my one tip for nailing it every time–Do the opposite.  What do I mean by that? Let’s see: This blazer is long–so pairing it with a short dress (I can’t say enough good things about this one–it’s so flattering!) worked perfectly. (This is why blazers also look adorable with shorts and skirts! I’m definitely pairing mine with my suede miniskirt and some OTK boots too!) This blazer is masculine–so pairing it with something feminine really hits the mark. (Feminine can also mean a pretty lace camisole, a hair bow, or feminine slingback flats!) This blazer is dressy–so pairing it with something more casual creates a really great contrast! (Casual can mean jeans–I’d go with form fitting skinnies or a pair of faux leather leggings! More on why below.) This blazer is a muted–subtle print, so pairing it with a bold printed shoe, like leopard, is an ideal contrast. (Bold could also mean these adorable deep red velvet booties that tie around the ankle–or even a swipe of red lipstick!) This blazer is loose and shapeless–so it should be paired with something form-fitting (the alternative is something that shows leg, as we solved above!) but if not a dress, you want to go with something form-fitting on the bottom. So, when you wear this to work–you’ll want to go with something like a ponte pant, rather than something a bit looser, like a trouser–make sense? See how well that works?! This is a trick that can help you get dressed EVERY DAY. It doesn’t just work for blazers! Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog May 7, 2019  Hii friends!  Today, I’m doing another styling session on Instagram stories with my friends Natalie and Connie! We haven’t done one in what feels like FOREVER, so I’m excited to be teaming up again today! We also have some newcomers who I think you’ll love, Cori from Dress Corilynn and Thuy from HeyThuy! Make sure to watch out for all our styling videos to go live at 12pm CST–where we’re all sharing our take on how to style white jeans!  Speaking of, I asked you guys on stories yesterday what you’d like me to focus on for a white jeans styling session, and got an OVERWHELMING response for “how to wear white jeans to work” and “how to wear white on white”–so I decided to tackle BOTH today–and style a super versatile white button down with white jeans–8 different ways that totally work in and out of the office!  I heard a lot of myths and questions about white jeans from you guys yesterday, so wanted to address a few of these upfront!  No, you should take some time to find the correct white jeans that flatter your body and order your correct size. Jeans that are one size too big are going to look ill fitting, bunchy, and you’ll have to hike them up all the time, therefore, you’ll probably never wear them because you aren’t confident in them.  I think you just haven’t found the right white jeans. Also, what drives me crazy is that we associate “flattering” with “thin”–and we have got to stop thinking that way. Thin does not mean flattering! Women of all sizes can and should feel good rocking a pair of white jeans.  White jeans ARE flattering. The right pair will accentuate your curves and make any outfit look more crisp, polished, and bright! Do you look SKINNIER in white jeans than you do in black jeans? No–of course not, darker colors are always more minimizing if that’s what you’re referring to, but doesn’t mean you don’t look beautiful in them and that you shouldn’t wear them!  “There is no such thing as non see through white jeans”  Yes there are–I’m sharing two pairs with you today. ?They both have great return policies so there is no reason why you shouldn’t try them!  With the right white jeans, it doesn’t matter what color underwear you’re wearing. But if you are still in the market for some invisible underwear, look for a super thin, raw-edge thong that matches your skin tone as closely as possible. These are great and come in multiple shades of nude!  You just need to be more cognizant in general–put your napkin on your lap, don’t sit on dirty benches, etc. Also, wash your jeans immediately if you get something on them. I spot treat with Shout and then soak in Oxyclean–Oxyclean is magic. (FYI I’m trying to switch to cleaner laundry products but have yet to find good clean stain-fighting alternatives!)  Okay! Let’s jump into the outfits, yeah!? For easy reference, you can shop all of the items I used to style these 8 outfits by clicking on the photos below.  Want more details? See my sizing notes, details, etc for each item below.     (Right) Available at Nordstrom and Madewell. (Madewell has extended sizes!) These I found because you guys raved about them so much! I went through SO MANY pairs of see through jeans before these. I can wear these with black underwear even and no see through! Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog October 31, 2014   Photography by the incredible Cassandra Eldridge It’s been a year since my first outfit post (okay, like a year and a week because I’ve been too busy to get my you-know-what together over the past several days). A year? Already? That’s bananas. I consider my first “outfit post” as my blogiversary (which is officially the most embarrassing phrase I’ve used in awhile). Why? Because that’s the first time I actually told the world that GG existed. In all her glory, with her ramshackle aesthetic on an old Blogger platform, completely riddled with iPhone photos. The product of a girl who just discovered a Cannon Rebel but had never heard of “manual” mode. That was me, 1 year ago. And how much GG has changed my life since then.  A year ago, I worked at at advertising agency. I loved my team, liked my job, but I craved more creativity. I dreamed of making something out of my own tiny slice of the internet, but really viewed it as that little wobbly Dominoes breadstick that nobody wants, rather than a real slice of pie. Not that long ago, none of my friends would have described me as the “fashionable” one. My best friends still remember the days where I used to wear giant gold belts over button down shirts (I guess my love of gold has never wavered) in attempts to hide the freshman 15 I gained in college. They even made a sorority skit about my embarrassing belts. That happened, yes. But then I developed a love of style, and then turned it into a blog. I’m not even entirely able to pinpoint why and how that thought ever crossed my mind in the first place.  



(adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});
 But in just 12 months time, this little blog has been more fun than I ever thought possible, and changed my life in more ways than one (more ways than 100, if we’re being honest). Here are some of my favorite moments of the past year:     And how surreal it was to be shooting GG’s “birthday” shoot, with Cassandra, a ridiculously talented professional photographer I would’ve never imagined I’d get to work with, let alone call her my friend. In Debbi Lily’s gorgeous studio space, A Perfect Event, no less — I never wanted to leave (if you’re looking for a party venue by the way, this is SO your place.)  And you. The person who cared enough to scroll all the way to the end of my sappy, rambling post. Thank you, most of all, for the amazing support. This blog is still so small, and such a work in progress, but I feel so lucky that you’ve stuck with me along the way! I hope you’ll hang around to see what else is in store for year two! Bodysuits, my friends, are one of those trends. At first I just thought they were for those really tan 22-year-old Coachella-attending beauties–but it isn’t so! I’ll prove it to you.  If you’re on the fence, OR, you are 100% on team bodysuit, but need some inspiration on ways to wear one–you’re in luck, because today, I’m talking ALL about ’em–sharing my favorites, and four outfits to copy next time you pull yours out of your closet!  First up–let’s identify the right bodysuit for you! (Maybe that’s why I like it? ) It’s sexy without trying too hard–which I think is the only way to go no matter what your age.  Fit: I would recommend sizing up–I got an XS (which is what I always am) and if it were any smaller, it would be too small–the shirt is very low and I think it’s just because the larger size would’ve been a bit roomier in the torso. Sunday we had a few friends over for the Superbowl, which was so fun! One of our favorite parts of our new place is that there is actually room to entertain! I made buffalo chicken in the crockpot and set up a buffalo chicken taco bar–it was so easy–if you’re ever looking for a no-fuss way to feed a casual crowd, I can’t say enough good things. All you do is combine chicken breasts in the crock pot with 1 bottle of hot sauce. I also sprinkled in some garlic powder and seasoning salt. Cook it on low for 5-7 hours, shred it, and put it back in the crock pot, mix it well with the sauce, and serve with flour tortillas and your favorite toppings. (I also made pickled onions and cabbage slaw to go on top!) Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog May 14, 2015   Blazer: TJ Maxx (similar here, here, and here) // Jeans: Henry & Belle // Sweater: Old (identical here, also love this one) // Scarf: Zara (also love this one and this one) // Backpack: Vera Bradley  Happy Thursday! Today’s post is a throwback, shot during our Ireland trip! We took these while walking around the city of Dublin, and this was one of my favorite outfits of the trip. I was typically wearing some version of it almost every day! I think there’s a secret sauce when it comes to the perfect travel outfit–heres my take:  Dark skinny jeans: I brought two pairs of jeans on my Ireland trip, but this is the pair I reached for over and over! Dark skinnies are perfect for travel for several reasons: they don’t show dirt (which you’ll inevitably attract anywhere in Europe) and they’re skinny, so they fit inside your boots, and look just as great with sneakers. (VS a pair of flares, for example, that won’t fit into your boots.) They also don’t drag on the ground, which would be very problematic for walking (again, flares, not such a great idea for travel.) Favorite pairs: Henry & Belle, J. Brand, Paige, Madewell, Forever21 A navy blazer: I wore this navy blazer over and over. It’s chic, polished, and makes any outfit look a little more put together. Why navy over black? I felt that it went with more, and I think navy looks much prettier on most skin tones than black does. I love J.Crew Factory, Asos, and Loft, which always typically have a great blazer selection. For warmer months, go for a lighter weight version in linen! Stripes: This sounds weird, but stripes are perfect for travel! Striped basics are so much cuter than solid colors, and the pattern disguises dirt really well. I brought several striped items on this trip and I wore them all on constant rotation. Stripped sweaters, dresses, tees, everything! A blanket scarf: An oversized scarf is great for any trip, because it adds extra warmth, makes your outfit more stylish, and also acts as a blanket on freezing cold planes, hotels and so forth. Boots: If you’re going to Europe in the Spring, Fall or Winter, boots are an absolute must! Make sure the pair you bring has a leather sole, so they’re comfortable and can endure plenty of wear and tear. I loved this lace up pair (they’re vintage!) because I could switch out the laces depending on my mood! Bright lipstick: When all else fails, red lipstick will always make you feel more put together! I love MAC matte lipstick in Lady Danger, and Younique lip stain!  Bag: Whenever you’re traveling, you want to go with either a cross body purse or a backpack. Cross body versions are safer from pick pockets (the one downside to a backpack, you can’t see if someone is reaching into it behind you), but they do get heavy, bulky, and don’t hold as much. I absolutely loved this Vera Bradley version–it held SO much, its perfect for day but chic enough to go out with at night. The perfect travel bag in my opinion. It also has several pockets, which are great for storage.

Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog September 19, 2019   This post is sponsored by Barbour in honor of their 125th anniversary!  Barbour Jacket (c/o Barbour–wearing US size 4. Liner vest also available for extra warmth! ), Jeans (Run TTS–wearing size 25), Sweater (TTS, wearing small), Sunglasses, Similar Chelsea Boots  By the time you read this, I THINK we should have made it to Spain by now! Fingers crossed that we had an uneventful flight! (Knowing us, we took full advantage of the “free wine” international flight policy and cried laughing for a full 7 hours binge-listening to our hilarious favorite podcast.)  Today, I am SO excited to be teaming up with another one of my favorite brands–Barbour–to celebrate their 125th anniversary! Did you know that they are still a family-owned brand, five generations later? Being a history nerd, I think the heritage of the brand has always been something that I was drawn to.  One particular piece of Barbour history stood out to me though–that I didn’t know until I watched this beautifully done film on the brand. (Which I’d highly recommend watching!) And that is the total girl boss story of Dame Margaret Barbour in particular. (Can she write a memoir, please?)  A few years after they fell in love and were married–John (the then fourth-generation Barbour), died suddenly at the age of 29, leaving her a very young widowed, single parent. As a teacher (note, she did not become Dame Margaret until later on in life!) she had no business background, and no involvement in the business at the time of his death. Determined to carry on his legacy, she stepped in, immersing herself in every aspect of the business. From learning how to make jackets to working the storeroom, answering the phones, meeting with customers in the field–you name it. She threw herself into it. Eventually, she became the force that is responsible for turning the Barbour jacket into the fashion icon that it is today.  I have always adored the brand, and working with them over the years has always been a career highlight of mine, but I was especially touched and felt even more drawn to them after hearing her story.  So, to bring this full circle–to celebrate their 125th anniversary, Barbour released a special collection of jackets, and reached out to me (!) to ask if I would wear one of them to help promote the occasion. (Isn’t that such an honor!?) So in this post today, I am excited to tell you ALL about this amazing jacket– If the name “Beaufort jacket” sounds familiar to you, that’s because it’s one of the most iconic men’s Barbour jackets. Originally cut for shooting, they are a relaxed fit and have a TON of pockets. You will never need to carry a purse when you have this jacket on–it fits everything! And guess who it was designed by? My girl–DAME MARGARET.  It turns out, she was inspired on a trip to France in the 1970’s–and designed this jacket as a result! It was later worn by Helen Mirren in her role in The Queen.  This newly-released Beaufort that I’m wearing here is based on that same classic design she created, with some slightly updated, feminine twists–like beautiful gold hardware and tartan cuff (which is optional–you can turn it up or leave it down if you prefer) with velvet detailing. It truly is a beautiful jacket. If you’ve loved the look of a classic Barbour but wanted something with a little bit more pizazz, this is definitely your coat!  When I wear this jacket, I feel like I’m channeling my inner Dame Margaret Barbour, and that feels pretty special!     I know that’s probably exactly what you’re thinking, so I’ll list some similarities and differences between this and the Beadnell, which is the other classic Barbour I own. (I have both a waxed and a quilted Beadnell. For these purposes, we’ll compare to the waxed version as that’s the most similar and most popular!)  This jacket has the same waxed coating that makes it an essential tool for braving all sorts of weather. It is the “Sage” color (i.e. a deep blue-green) that is a classic Barbour color. The Beadnell, for example, also comes in sage depending on the retailer you choose to purchase from. Like many Barbour jackets, it has the ability to add a zip-in liner, as well as a snap-on hood. It also has the fantastic slanted “hand warming pockets” that you expect from Barbour–ensuring no cold wind touches your hands!  The design details listed above are really what set this jacket apart and make it different than other classic Barbour coats, but here are some other notable differences vs. the Beadnell:  First, is the design–which is much roomier than the Beadnell, for example. Whereas the Beadnell is cut to be form-fitting, the Beadnell is designed to be more of a relaxed, longer fit.  In terms of warmth, I think that it happens to be warmer than the Beadnell, especially if you choose to purchase a zip-in liner (pictured below–which also happen to be adorable when worn alone as a vest!)  Another warm differentiator is that it has super cozy sleeve details that ensure no cold air gets in through your sleeves! (Basically, like sweater cuffs that are attached to the coat!) Due to these differences and the fact that the jacket is a special edition, the price tag is higher. It’s at $545 for the Beaufort and $414 for the Beadnell.  Is there a right or wrong choice? Of course not! Any Barbour jacket is a fantastic jacket–but I hope this helps decide which one is best for you!        Huge thanks to Barbour for including me in your 125th Anniversary Celebration and for sponsoring this post. It’s always such an honor to work with you! And thank YOU, my main gals, for supporting the brands that help keep this blog up and running! More questions on Barbour coats? Get this widget. Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog January 4, 2019   Welp! Ready or not, 2019 is officially here! Just like everyone else, I have some fitness goals I’d like to achieve and fine-tune this year–and I’m guessing you do as well! I love this time of year and really look forward to hitting the reset button.  The end of the year–November and December in particular–are always really busy for me, and the first thing that I let go is my workouts when I don’t have enough hours in the day. I know that most people will tell you that letting your workouts fall by the wayside is a terrible thing and that you should always prioritize getting to the gym–but honestly, something’s gotta give–and I truly just didn’t have any other way to find more hours in the day. For me, allowing myself to get enough sleep and enough time to relax and give my brain a break is more important mentally than working out. I don’t regret it–it’s what’s necessary for me to do sometimes in the super crazy seasons, and being OK with not being able to workout rather than beating myself up about it was much better for my personal sanity. (So, if you’re in the same boat–stop feeling guilty about it!)  However, that crazy period of life has passed (whew!) and I’m looking forward to getting into a routine again. However, that’s not to say that I actually LIKE working out. I don’t. ?But I LOVE the way I feel and look when I work out regularly, and it’s always going to be a priority for me to strive for a good workout/life balance. But I still need motivation to kick my butt in gear ? Do you feel that way too? If you’re also lacking motivation, here are the three tips that have made the BIGGEST difference in my fitness motivation, accomplishing my fitness goals, and helped to make working out a bigger part of my life:     I’ve found that when I’ve taken the time to sit down on a Monday morning and schedule when I’m going to work out–I stick to it much better.  I actually go through the Orangetheory and CorePower schedules and figure out which classes fit in best with my days, and I literally create meetings titled “Yoga” or “OTF” on my calendar. I also set a 30 minute “meeting” right beforehand that is labeled “get ready for yoga” so I don’t skip a workout simply because I didn’t have enough time to get ready and get there on time.  For whatever reason, this little trick really helps my mindset and makes it harder to say, “oh, I’ll just catch the later class…” even though I know it will never happen! Also, if you’re one of those people who likes to work out in the morning but can never drag yourself out of bed, I HIGHLY recommend the app “Kiwake”–it’s an alarm that is impossible to snooze–it will definitely ensure you make it to that 7am workout class!   SERIOUSLY. Call me ridiculous but this WORKS, you guys.  When I look forward to putting on a cute workout outfit, I look forward to working out in general a whole lot more. I think the difference between wearing a schleppy old college t-shirt to work out and a cute, put-together workout outfit results in a huge shift in anyone’s attitude–especially mine! It’s the same principle that applies to getting dressed for anything, really. If you look crappy, you feel crappy, so personally, I think it’s really important to invest in some good workout outfits that you feel really confident in!  Good news on that front: The three activewear essentials I’m wearing in this post are all on sale right now at Lord & Taylor as part of their “New Year, New You” up to 40% off activewear sale! Definitely give it a look to see if anything marked down catches your eye. Now is a perfect time to invest in those staples I just mentioned. Here are my faves:  I absolutely love this tank! It’s so soft and lightweight–most of my workouts either consist of Orangetheory or hot yoga, so the lighter the fabric, the better, because I’m a baby and overheat very easily ?It’s such a cute top and you really can’t beat the price! (I also love this simple workout tank that is also on sale! You can never have too many white or black workout tops!)  I don’t think you can own too many pairs of black workout leggings, right!? They are always my workout staple of choice. I love this pair for many reasons–one being the price, another being how thick they are. They hold you in in all the right places (so they’re ideal for higher impact workouts) and there’s no show-through! (This pair is the same brand and also cute if you like a little more zazz!)  I love cute hoodie that I can throw on after a workout and wear to brunch or run errands. This one comes in so many colors, I loved the cropped element and the velvet coated drawstring! So much cuter than a regular old sweatshirt! Plus, it’s less than $20! It also comes in so many colors–I really wanted the dusty lilac color but it was sold out when I placed my order–now it’s re-stocked though, so somebody has to order it and send me a photo so I can live vicariously through you ? It’s made by the brand ASKYA which I hadn’t heard of before–but definitely want to try more of their items! I also love this furry faux sherpa half-zip that is on sale for only $30! This cropped mock-neck for $27 is also super cute. Also, right now, ASKYA sports bras are on crazy sale–starting at $10!   Don’t get me wrong, there are some great at-home workouts that work really well for a lot of people, but they just aren’t something I’m able to stick with long-term. (I still do them sometimes too when I’m in a pinch! I wrote about my two favorites here!) but I don’t have enough willpower to push myself nearly as much as I will push myself in a studio setting. I’m just not that kind of person. (Which is why joining regular gyms has never worked for me.)  Orangetheory and Corepower yoga–and I absolutely love both of them. Is this expensive? Yes. But I get a hell of a lot more out of belonging to these two than I EVER would paying for a gym membership that results in me literally pouring money down the drain. (Honestly, I just don’t push myself working out on my own in a gym, nor see nearly the type of results I do at these two studios). I wrote a HUGE Orangetheory fitness review and results post right here because I get so many questions. I do Orangetheory for the aesthetic benefits–meaning, I have NEVER seen changes in my body like the ones I’ve seen from Orangetheory. Period, the end. If you’re serious about getting into shape, I wholeheartedly believe there is no other workout at ANY gym that is going to get you the results that OTF does.  On the flipside, I do yoga at Corepower for fun, for the mental benefits of yoga, and because it’s an excellent low-impact workout (and lot’s of stretching) that perfectly compliments OTF. I do C2 (hot power yoga) classes exclusively.  Aside from the results that come along with studio memberships, I think the community that comes along with belonging to a studio is one of the biggest draws to get my butt in the door. And I don’t mean this in the sense that you should always have a workout buddy to keep you accountable, but having a few friendly faces at your studio can make a big difference!  When I make friends with my yoga instructors, or I can count on my Orangetheory Trainers to DM me on Instagram like, “Ummm where have you been ?” it’s a whole new draw to working out. When you have a community to look forward to (or you know people will notice when you aren’t there) it helps keep you accountable, not to mention, really gives you something to look forward to! So, if you’ve been on the fence about joining a studio vs a gym (is it worth the money? Will you stick to it?) consider this me giving you that extra push. I really don’t think you’ll regret it!  We did one GG reader meet up at Orangetheory in 2018–it was SO fun and such a great way to meet new friends–I’m definitely planning to do more fitness related meet-ups in 2019, so make sure you’re following me on Instagram, because that’s where I’ll be posting about upcoming opportunities!  I hope these tips help you as much as they help me! I feel like I’ve literally been through every “style” phrase known to man. Except for goth. I’ve never been goth. Thankfully for my mother’s sake, I never went down that route. Although I did go through a “sk8er” phase with purple vans and parachute pants. Those were good days.  It’s like I walked into a hat shop and played duck duck goose– trying on the “preppy” hat, “edgy” hat, “trendy” hat, “classic” hat, and kind of worked through them all with some good old trial and error.  Have you done that too?   One of those major “hats” is jewelry. As you’ve probably noticed by now, I’ve become a bit of a jewelry minimalist. A couple years ago, I really loved anything with major sparkle. Arm parties were my favorite kinds of parties. I attribute part of this, of course, to statement jewelry being really big back then. (Not that it’s out now, I still think there’s a time and a place for it!) But these days, I think simple is best. I absolutely love the simplicity of dainty gold jewelry–it’s both understated and feminine.  So when British jewelry brand, Monica Vinader, reached out to me to work together, I took one look at her jewelry and squealed a resounding “yes!” I love working with awesome small brands who are doing big things, so hopefully you guys are excited to be introduced to her designs as I was!  Here I’m wearing the Fiji Bracelet–in gold, but it comes in a bunch of different colors (rose gold, too–I love the detail of the metal drawstring fastener!) The Riva diamond ring is also the perfect subtle statement, along with the matching Riva diamond studs. They go with literally everything, year round! I especially love jewelry like this for travel–you can leave it on the entire time, and never have to change it! It’s the perfect accent to everything from casual jeans to flirty dresses.  If you want to check out her designs in person, make sure to stop by the Monica Vinader trunk show at Nordstrom Michigan Avenue on May 7th. (All those details below!) Purchase anything at the trunk show, and receive customized engraving free of charge! If you can’t make it to the event, you’ll definitely want to peruse all of her collections online and at Nordstrom and Nordstrom.com! (Just in time for Mother’s Day!)  Speaking of pairing perfectly with flirty dresses, I styled my MV pieces with my new favorite LRD. (Little Red Dress!) It’s off the shoulder (I swear everything I’ve purchased in the last month is off the shoulder, whoops!) and I’ve been wearing it on repeat. It’s great for everything from casual shopping to a bachelorette party. Topped off with my new favorite boater hat (I’ve been wanting one of them for years, and I’m so excited to wear this one all summer!) and espadrilles.  And yes, now that you mention it, my outfit does match my new bike! Okay, so, I really did not have any intention of shooting my latest weeknight dinner experiment with you, but after I shared it on Instagram stories (as I often do, you know, share my recipe experiments) so many of you wanted the recipe! So, I did what any other completely lazy non-food blogger would do–I tried to make my next day’s leftovers look somewhat presentable by covering them with beautifully sliced avocados, got out my tripod, took 100 totally failed attempts of myself eating said leftover enchiladas and got…two normal looking photos. Actually, I probably wouldn’t classify the above as “normal” because if you look closely you can see my haphazard bra strap AND a rogue corn kernel falling mid-air as the photo was being taken. I feel the need to tell you this because I could’ve chosen to photoshop them out, but I chose drinking wine instead. Priorities. ? I also don’t know why I chose to put them on such a tiny plate. I literally have 3 different sizes of plates to choose from. Still I choose the miniature version. I don’t know, you guys. This further proves I should never be a food blogger. This is my long-winded way of telling you that if you thought these photos were taken by my adoring husband on a leisurely Sunday afternoon of enchilada eating…you were mistaken. ? #LIFE. Amiright?! So–I feel like I’ve kind of become this crazy Trader Joe’s lady? So much so that I feel like my blog should maybe be renamed “The Golden Girl and How She Spent All Her Money Grocery Shopping.” The thing is, I know you get it. t’s actually insanely heartwarming to know that I have curated a community that is as obsessed with TJ’s as I am. We’re all so incredibly basic but we really own it, you know? Like last time I was checking out and the checker handed me my bottle of Kombucha, rather than putting it in the bag, and said, “you look like the kind of girl who wants to drink this in the car…” ?? He’s right–we are who we are! Anyway, as you likely know by now if you follow me on Instagram stories, I am trying to do a lot more plant-based meals these days. (You can read all about my plant-based-diet experience in this post!) One day I decided to get REAL creative and chop up one of my favorite TJ’s veggie burgers and use it in place of meat in a taco, and it was REAL good. Then I tried it in a salad bowl with similar success, which lead me to post [by popular demand] my “recipe” for my Trader Joe’s Cowboy Quinoa Burger Salad Bowls (even though it’s not ACTUALLY a recipe. There is no measuring involved and it really just involves pulling various items out of freezers and/or pre-packaged bags–you know, TJ’s style.) Then, I had a major craving for enchiladas. But here’s the thing–all the plant-based enchilada recipes you find have beans in them. Sadly, I am very finicky when it comes to beans, and I do not want them in my enchiladas. Also then there was the issue that I dearly love enchiladas suizas (which have sour cream) slathered with cheese. Not exactly things I’m trying to eat a lot of these days. So–I thought to myself, what would happen I replaced the cream and cheese with cashew crema…and the meat with Quinoa Cowboy Burger?! (REALLY GOOD THINGS. That’s what happens.)   Corn tortillas (however many you use just depends on the size of the pan and how many people you’re feeding–see notes below). Your favorite enchilada sauce (I prefer verde sauce, which I’ve purchased in a can/jar and also fresh. In this instance, I used a fresh verde salsa. It’s truly up to you.) Onions and your favorite peppers (I used a mix of bell and poblano, sliced and roasted in the oven). Again, you can eyeball this, it just depends on how many people you’re feeding. Frozen corn–just eyeball it. Put as much corn as you like. TJ’s Quinoa Cowboy Burgers–1 burger per person “Cheesy” cashew crema–I sort of riff off of Minimalist Baker’s recipe (she shares three ways to do cashew cheese in her post! It’s really awesome and informative!) but really, it’s a taste as you go thing! I use a Blendtec blender to blend it all together! Avocado to top  Fresh cilantro, to top  If you’ve ever read one of my recipe-ish posts, you know I don’t measure things. This is why I’m not a food blogger. However, I also am passionate about cooking and truly believe in developing the skills you need to not use a recipe when you cook. When you cook by instinct, you’ll always be able to make anything taste good! Anyway, to start, heat up a cast iron pan (if you have one) with a drizzle of oil and toss in those quinoa burgers. You want to saute them, chopping them up as you go so it becomes the consistency of ground beef. The idea here is to make it extra crispy and chewy. If you don’t get them crispy then they become soggy and more of a beany texture and nobody likes soggy enchilada filling. (Or do they?) When that’s cooking, you can whip up your cashew sauce using a blender. Again, you’ll find the recipe I like to use here (you’ll want to follow her “queso” instructions. I added a bit of my favorite hot sauce! When your quinoa cowboy “meat” is done, throw in some pre-roasted veggies. Eyeball this–there’s no right or wrong ratio, whatever looks good to you! To me, the more veggies, the merrier! Mix it all in together. Now comes the enchilada assembly. I honestly prefer my enchiladas layered like a lasagna–I know this is NOT the traditional way to do enchiladas but it’s how they’re made in the Loftus household. Here’s how I do it: Using a non-stick baking pan, spray some non-stick cooking spray, and lay down a bit of your enchilada sauce. (This ensures the bottom tortilla doesn’t burn!) Then, do a bottom layer of corn tortillas. Then follow with your “meat” and veggie mixture, followed by your enchilada sauce, and a drizzle of your crema. Be liberal with the sauce, the tortillas will soak a lot of it up. You don’t want dry enchiladas! Put another layer of tortillas on top, and repeat the process until all your mixture is used up! Top with more enchilada sauce and more crema, and pop into a 350 degree oven for 10-15 minutes. (Once more–use your best judgement. When they’re golden and bubbly, you’re good to go!) Let cool slightly, and serve with another drizzle of sauce and crema on top (if you’d like) and sliced avocados, cilantro, and I always love a sprinkle of chili powder or cayenne pepper.   Enjoy with my favorite Mexican beverage: Ice cold Mexican beer poured over ice with tons of lime juice and a hefty pinch of Tajin. Bottoms up! I’ve been getting SO many questions on my favorite wool coat–the J.Crew cocoon coat, so I thought I’d dedicate today’s post to diving into an in-depth review. (Plus, you know, I’ll spill the details on everything else I’m wearing too!)  I owe my love of the J.Crew Cocoon coat (and many other things) to Kelly. I borrowed her grey cocoon coat many many years ago and was SHOCKED at how warm it was. Before then, I thought all non puffer coats were just for looks and not for warmth–luckily, this one is actually for both!  We shot these photos in Lincoln Park last week, and I got to hang and play with Emma a little bit afterwords before heading to Eataly to check out their latest restaurant, BAITA, and take a Gnocchi cooking class! They are one of my FAVORITE partners to work with! (Also, make sure you enter my instagram giveaway–I’m giving away two tickets to their Gnocchi making class!)  Emma is getting SO big. She has such a big personality and she refers to me as “Uncle Jess” ? which is my favorite thing ever. She had just woken up from her nap and gave me the biggest hug. My heart!  Anyway, okay, the coat. That’s what we’re talking about today. (Did I mention that Emma has her own Cocoon coat?!)  So–let’s jump in with some facts and FAQ’s  The J.Crew Cocoon coat does run big–I would suggest sizing down. I’m usually a 0 or 2 in coats and I ordered a size 0 and I still have room to layer underneath it.  You’re funny ? No, sadly, it will not. You will not wear this coat when there is snow on the ground in February and you need to walk to work. HOWEVER, it’s definitely warm enough to wear in probabblyyy 30 degrees and above–and you’ll always wear it out at night all winter long (as long as you’re not walking–it’s a great coat when you want to look nice, warm, and you’re pretty much going from your door into an Uber). Pilling is caused by friction and rubbing of material–which is why you’ll often find that coats pill under arms (because you swing your arms when you walk). I have not personally had problem with pilling but I have heard from others who have. Honestly, this is something that happens with most coats–just buy a de-piller and you’re fine! (You can also use an old razor, but I don’t think it works as well!) Tissue Turtleneck: Duh. When am I not wearing one of these? They are the BEST. They are super thin (like a very thin t-shirt!) and I love that they’re form-fitting (not chunky) turtlenecks. My favorites are the striped versions ?? I own them in both Small and XS–the one I’m wearing here is XS. I would say it runs true to size, I always order either XS or Small depending on how I want it to fit. if you want it snug like this, go with the smaller size. If you want it a bit looser, go with the larger size!  Black skinny jeans: These jeans are from American Eagle ?? You first saw me style them in my Fall Weekend Capsule Wardrobe–if you don’t want to spend a lot but want some super soft, stretchy skinny jeans–these are AMAZING. They run small though, so size up from your normal size! Everlane Day Boots: O-M-G-you guys. These freaking boots. Helllooo and happy Friday!




(adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});
 By the time you’re reading this, I’ll likely be en route to Cancun or maybe even by the pool already  (YESSSSS!) I’m happy to report that I’ll be shooting quite a few outfits while I’m there, so you’ll be able to get a little break from all the cold weather wear! Also, it makes me feel better that we’ll be taking a California trip in February–so at least there’s another frigid weather break on the horizon. Neal just started covering California for work, so I will obviously be tagging along with those trips as much as I can! Thinking we’ll be in the LA area most of the time on our first trip out there, so if you have any suggestions–let me know! (Helpful side note: He decided to switch to the Southwest credit card for business expenses, which means he’ll get a companion pass next year–AKA I can fly for free with him! I’d definitely recommend looking into that if you have a business credit card! Counting down the days until that happens!) In other news, I’m popping by Kelly’s soon to say hi before we leave! We usually spend several hours per week together, but with the holidays, it’s been almost a month! WAH! I also dropped my phone on the stairs (again) walking out of the house to the coffee shop this morning and pretty much finished off what was already a struggling-to-hold-on phone case. An hour later, we were g-chatting and she sent me a photo of a brand new phone case she found in her desk and asked if I wanted it–haha! (It’s like we have ESPN or something…)  With the holiday down time, Neal and I got a chance to try out some cool new places that recently opened in our neighborhood–Publican Anker and Hotel Robey! BOTH of which you need to put on your list! If you’re a Chicago foodie you might freak out a little when I say this, but Publican’s burger is better than Au Cheval’s. (GASP!) I went there, and I stand firmly by my statement. I think it’s one of the best burgers in Chicago. The avocado salad was also to die for. I also happened to pass Hotel Robey on my way to yoga a couple weeks back and did a double take. I had NO idea that a hotel was opening in Wicker Park. (Basically a hotel desert.) They have the cutest cafe on the bottom floor! While I haven’t tried the food at the cafe yet, what I did check out was the 2nd floor lounge, which serves coffee and booze. (Excellent combinations when you’re getting some work done while on winter break.) It’s an awesome place to do some work. Neal met me later and we wrapped up some work stuff over a couple beers. It was so much fun! We made friends with our server, who is the food and beverage manager, and she took us upstairs to show us their rooftop bar. (Thanks Kaylee!) You guys, it’s one of the coolest views of the Chicago skyline that exists. It’s easily the highest view in Wicker Park, so you see the city from a whole different perspective. It was packed, and its really small, so if you want to check it out, I suggest going early! The hotel is also really nice and the prices look pretty affordable, so if you’re visiting and looking to stay outside of downtown Chicago (which I’d definitely recommend!) you should look into it! I love wearing my suede leggings on outings like these because they feel like sweatpants (they’re warm, too!) but look way cooler than jeans! (Don’t you love when that happens?) When it comes to winter fashion staples, these really can’t be beat! I also love the look of them paired with my riding boots! This amazing sweater JUST got re-stocked in all colors and now it’s on sale! (I love when that happens!) It’s 100% cashmere and is seriously so soft. It’s such a classic staple!    For work: Yes, you CAN make these work for a business-casual setting (well, of course, not ALL offices, but many of them) with a crisp white button down and classic D’Orsay pumps. Tie a silk scarf around your neck for extra credit! I love that this one has both black and navy, which means you can wear it with pretty much everything. (If you’re wondering how to tie your scarf, I did a post on that here!) For dinner: Pair them with a pretty blouse (I LOVE the color of this one and its sleeve details) and black OTK boots (at first I thought the suede on suede thing would look weird, but with the color difference, it looks great!) I’ve been wearing mine with my new Lowland boots I got for Christmas and LOVE the combo, but my budget-friendly OTK boots look just as great, too! For weekend brunch: Style with a cozy oversized cardigan, casual tee (this one is my year-round go-to), and sneakers!    P.S. Remember, if you’re bored this weekend, follow along on our Mexico trip via Instagram and Insta stories! ;-P  Photos by Jules Kennedy Filed Under: Outfits, Style

Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog September 28, 2016   Hey guys, It’s Neal here with today’s post.   Jess usually likes to keep me behind the lens or only in pictures, so tell her to give me a few more guest writing opportunities if you can tolerate my writing. I’m here today to talk about the really masculine topic of “Fall style.” Specifically, football style, which is something I can really get behind. Early fall has long been my favorite time of year (and it has NOTHING to do with Pumpkin Spice ANYTHING.) The craziness of summer is finally over, and my focus can get back to what is most important: family, friends and football (obviously). 



(adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});
  
 My dad has been a Bears season ticket holder for 21 years, and despite some up and down play on the field, some of my best memories are going to the stadium with him.  Jess and I went on our first real date on a mid-September afternoon, and I still remember how perfect that day was.  It had almost everything to do with her, but changing leaves and fall air really helped put that day up there with some of the best days of my life.  Ok. This is a post about football fashion, so I’ll stop getting so sentimental, but in case you can’t tell, I think this is the best time of year. Jess and I like to spend our fall weekends wearing better clothes (layers, sweaters > t-shirt and shorts), drinking better (darker beer & cider > light beer & cocktails) and eating better (Jess is a great cook year round, I just get excited for soup, chili, and tailgate food). As I sit here and write this I am already looking forward to the next time we get to find a cozy Wicker Park bar or have friends over for another NFL Sunday. As nice as my previous paragraph sounds to me, there is something that I have not yet mentioned: I’m a die-hard Bears fan, and somehow, some way, Jess wound up a Packers fan.  The whole “house divided” thing is real – and it has not been kind to me thanks to the poor play of the Bears these last few seasons.  I have not held much of the bragging rights since we started dating, but when Levi’s approached us about doing a joint feature, my thought was “hey orange and blue is a better look than green and yellow – I’m in!”  If you can’t beat them, try to out-dress them.    If you have been reading Jess’ blog these last few months, you know that we have grown up quite a bit lately.  (Getting married, buying a house, yada yada.) I can say the same thing about my style – it has evolved a lot as I’ve hit my upper 20’s, and that includes my gameday wardrobe. I’ve always worn Levi’s jeans (as you can see in the photos), but the Bears denim trucker jacket ($108 – levi.com) and flannel ($78 – levi.com) qualify as some of my “new-and-improved” wardrobe items.  I enjoy being well dressed for any occasion, so when the Bears are playing, I prefer to look good supporting them versus the whole “Super Fan” look.  (DAAA BEARS.) The flannel is awesome – soft and warm but not too warm, so you can layer it.  It fits true to size, isn’t boxy or baggy, but also not skin tight.  The detail of the logo is also really nice quality (unlike that garbage you find online or outside the stadium) because while it’s clearly a Bears shirt, it’s also stylish enough for any other occasion that a great flannel calls for.  The jacket is one of the most unique pieces in my wardrobe.  Just like the flannel, it’s well made, has great detailing, and has a great fit.  It’s perfect to throw on if I’m meeting my buddies at the bar to watch a game, and warm enough for a tailgate or early fall games at Soldier Field with my dad. If you’re like me and think you can’t pull off the “denim on denim” look, I say go for it.  I liked mixing 2 different shades of denim, and it frees you up to get colorful with your flannels. (Jess’ note: spoken like a true #InstagramHusband). If you are looking to upgrade your guy’s gameday wardrobe, a classic American brand like Levi’s is the place to make that happen.     Big thanks to Levi’s for sponsoring this post and for the sweet game day gear. Thank you for supporting the brands that help support this blog, and I hope you know how much I appreciate your support of Jess!  Your readership and interaction keep us going!
