Have you watched either?! Anyway, back with another outfit post we shot at the lake! We took this right before we left to go out to dinner and it was the perfect casual cozy outfit for the occasion! As the temperatures have started to get chilly I’ve started getting questions on layering–particularly, how to layer without looking frumpy and bulky. So, I thought today would be a good day for a lesson  I’ve said it 100 times and I’ll say it again, everyone needs one of these turtleneck tees! When you’re adding a ton of layers on and don’t want to look too bulky, it really makes a big difference if you start with form-fitting base layers. The reason for this is that they show off the shape of your body (so you don’t look like a box) but also add warmth, so when you add a loose cardigan (we’ll go into this one in a minute!) over the top, you can still see your figure underneath! Shop turtleneck tees:    The same goes for pants (again, more on those below)–the more baggy your layers are on top, the more form-fitting your bottom-half should be. As a good rule of thumb, your tops and bottoms should be opposites. For example:  Tight on top and tight on the bottom= “floozie,” as my mom would say. Baggy on top and baggy on bottom= Stacy and Kent’s latest What Not To Wear Victim (“OH MY GOSH she’s got a figure under there!? Who knew!”) See? Obviously the answer is, like most things in life–finding the appropriate balance. Now–back to the cardigan–it is SO. SO. Soft. I love that it’s longer in length–which is beautiful both aesthetically, and also helps to add a ton of warmth! The great part is that it’s only $89, and it comes in other colors too! I believe this is the first “oatmeal” colored sweater I’ve ever purchased, and I think it’s so pretty! (A nice mix between the only two colors I seem to wear lately, cream and camel ?) For height reference, I’m 5’6 and it hits right at my knee. Shop my cardi in all colors:    And, for the pants. Are you getting sick of seeing these velvet leggings yet? You told me you didn’t understand how to style them, so maybe I’ve taken it overboard with three recent posts in a row wearing them?! But the truth is, I never really take them off.  ? I truthfully believe they’re more versatile even than regular leggings because they look like real pants, and therefore, can be dressed up for ton’s of different occasions, or dressed down, as you see here! They are also as comfortable as pajamas, and warmer than regular leggings, too. Sizing: run TTS.  Let’s call it what it is–sometimes you can feel like the more layers you add on, the frumpier you look. This is the sad but unfortunate truth of living in a colder climate. It’s harder to not look like an old cat lady when you go outside. (Not that I’m knocking old cat ladies.) Here’s a trick that I use and I hope that it helps you too–opt for footwear with a bit of a pointed toe. (What? Why? That’s so random.) Yes, I know. But stick with me. It goes back to what I was saying above. Had I chosen a chunky, rounder toed riding boot here, for example, that came out past my calf, it would’ve added more bulk. But these booties (which are only $59 on sale, by the way) actually make the outfit look more chic and sophisticated because the pointed toes and bit of heel goes a long way to elongate the leg. In a way, they’re more “form-fitting” shoes, if you will. Additionally, another reason that ankle booties work well here is because the cardigan comes down to my knees, so wearing a boot that hit right at the knee would’ve made my legs look substantially shorter and cut off. (The exception to this rule? Over the Knee boots–which, because they come up so high, also help to elongate the legs.)     This lesson took so long for me to learn. For the longest time, I owned very few scarves–maybe one in a cute-but-doesn’t-go-with-anything-pink pattern and one in plain black. (Functional but boring.) I never looked at scarves as a way to add to my outfit. They were always an after-thought. Solely to keep warm–much like my beanies and gloves. Which obviously never matched my scarves or the rest of my outfit for that matter. As a result, I may have had a pretty outfit on underneath, but I always looked so schleppy and thrown together whenever I had to go outside. I dreaded getting dressed for winter because it made me look like a “What Not to Wear” victim. Tip: Invest a little money upfront on a a handful of versatile accessories in different neutral colors and patterns–you really don’t need that many! This scarf, for example,  is a great one because it’s very neutral and matches so many different outfits, but it’s still a cute, interesting pattern. (That, and it’s only $25!) I also have a few different pom pom beanies that I rotate between (black, cream, and camel are the most versatile) and same with gloves or mittens! Also, for scarf styling tips see how to wear a scarf multiple ways. When you do this, you’ll actually look forward to bundling up, because you’ll still feel a lot more confident and stylish when your accessories actually go with your outfit! Shop neutral accessories:        There is a laundry list of reasons why I love my Canada Goose coat, but aside from being the warmest coat I’ve ever found (reason #1) I love that it truly isn’t bulky like most other puffer coats out there. I have the Shelburne Parka, which designed to be form-fitting, and it’s a true treat to not look like a marshmallow every day from November through March. I’ve been getting a lot of questions about Canada Goose coats and whether or not they’re worth it, so I did a whole post diving into the specific reasons why I love the Canada Goose Shelburne Parka in this post. I won’t go into them all again here, but in short, it has so many features that other coats don’t have that ensure you stay as warm as possible. I never knew how warm I could feel in negative temps until I got this coat. It TRULY does make a difference. It’s definitely one of the most expensive items that I own. Honestly though, when you break it down to how many times per year I wear it, coupled with the fact that it will last for well over a decade–that breaks down into a pretttttyy cheap cost per wear–and well-worth it when you live somewhere that transforms into an arctic tundra each winter. If you’re wondering about sizing, they run true to size! I’m wearing an XS, because I like my coats to be fitted. I rarely wear too many layers under them (well, never more than you see me wearing here) because the coat is so warm you really don’t need any extra layers with it! Nordstrom has a huge selection of Canada Goose coats (and also happens to stock everything else I’m wearing in this post ?) The best part about making big purchases like winter coats there is that their return policy is incredible (plus free shipping both ways!) so you don’t have to worry about making an investment and not being 110% happy with it! Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog February 2, 2016  Original outfit post here  So, not sure if you’ve noticed this (PRETTTYYY sure you have) but I have a slight obsession with silk scarves.  Throw one on over any outfit and they add instant polish and a classic twist. Don’t get me wrong, I love a good blanket scarf too–but they just don’t have the same amount of charm. Vintage shops are a great place to score them on the cheap, but if you’re not into thrifting or don’t have the time, there are plenty of places to buy them new! They’re one accessory that you’ll truly have forever. There are also lot’s of varieties that come in cotton, with the same square shape. (See #7 below!)  To tie them, fold them into a triangle, and then tie like a bandanna! You can also roll them and wrap them around your neck (stewardess style!) I’ve also received several requests to do a tutorial, so be on the lookout for that soon.  In the meantime–happy shopping!

Hi guys! Happy Tuesday of Thanksgiving week, haha! Can you believe how fast November has flown!? HOW is this possible!? I’m really excited because my mom gets in tomorrow ?? She’s coming into town for Thanksgiving again this year and we’re so excited to have her! (Thankfully the cleaning lady came yesterday so for once my house is in order ?) Many of the items I’m wearing today are on major markdown (if you want to get started on your Black Friday shopping early!) Right now, Lord & Taylor is offering 40% sweaters–including cashmere starting at $49.99–and boots for women and men, too! Recently I asked you guys on Instagram stories what kind of topics you’d like to see this season on the blog–so many of you answered with “how to dress up sweaters” and “how to wear OTK boots with skirts”–so, you’re getting a double whammy lesson today ?Huzzah! This also happens to be the PERFECT Thanksgiving outfit–so if you’re not sure what to wear, I hope this sparks some ideas! Let’s jump in, shall we!? There are few wardrobe staples more classic than the cashmere sweater. I prefer mine to be slimmer fit, because a more tailored sweater is easier to dress up vs. a chunky one, which will always just be casual no matter what you pair it with. Lord & Taylor makes TONS of affordable cashmere sweaters, and right now–they’re 40% off! In addition to this turtleneck, also own their v-neck in black, which I’ll be styling in a few days–so stay tuned! Their cashmere sweaters come in over 28 different colors and they run true to size in my experience–I’m wearing a small but keep in mind it is a slimmer fit, so if you want it a bit looser you could consider sizing up. What I love about a cashmere sweater is that you can literally pair it with anything–trousers for work, with jeans, you name it! Camel and black are my two favorite sweater colors because I think they’re the easiest to dress up. Black, obviously, a given–the most universally flattering color, and also the easiest to transform from day to night. Camel, because it’s a beautiful color on any skin tone and I just think it makes anything you wear with it look instantly classier and polished!  As soon as I saw this BlankNYC corduroy skirt I fell in love! Not only is the color perfection (“burnt sienna” orangey-brown is definitely my favorite color as of late!) but the corduroy adds another textural element to any outfit–which goes a long way in adding more visual interest. I always love pairing tops and bottoms of similar color families (i.e. here, brown and burnt sienna are both browns) for a polished and put together look. I love that the skirt isn’t too terribly short, and it’s high-waisted, so it’s really flattering because it hits you at the thinnest part of your waist and emphasizes an hourglass shape! It would also look just as cute with tights when it gets super cold! It runs true to size. I get this question a lot, so here are a few rules of thumb– Make sure there is a little bit of space between the top of your boot and the hemline of your skirt. If your skirt hem falls below the top of your boot, this will just look frumpy and add extra pounds that aren’t actually there. Whereas if there’s a bit of skin showing in between, it will elongate the leg and make you look super chic and stylish! I always recommend Blondo boots–they are incredibly durable, and come waterproofed! So you get the look and feel of suede without having to worry about ruining them the first time you step out of the house! While I have a more expensive pair, my Blondos are what I reach for whenever the ground is wet, there is snow on the ground, it’s raining, etc. I’ve received so many messages from you guys who have purchased them on my recommendation and the reviews are ALWAYS glowing! Right now, all of Lord & Taylor’s boots are on sale–so definitely peruse their awesome selection while the sale is running! I’m always a big proponent of pattern in ANY scenario! In this case, this scarf adds the perfect dose of classic plaid to the outfit to make it feel seasonal and festive without being over the top. (And no–it’s not designer–it’s Lord & Taylor’s brand and it’s under $40! ??) I will admit, I haven’t done a lot of shopping at L&T in the past–for reasons I don’t know (!)–but that is definitely changing! I absolutely love their namesake “Lord and Taylor” label–everything they make is so affordable but beautiful, classic, and stylish. They also carry a lot of my favorite brands, and they run so many amazing promotions, where you can often snag them at a discount!  YOU GUYS it’s so cold. WAHH! Know what’s funny? When you move into a new house in the summer and you don’t know if it’s going to be freezing or warm when winter rolls around? Remember when I told you about my favorite fur blanket that I walk around under all day like the Revenant? Yeah. Haven’t taken it off yet today. I’m under the blanket, on my fur bean bag, next to the fire. ITS STILL FREEZING. Did you catch how I slipped in “fur bean bag” in there? Yeah. I have one. And I decided they’re back. Pottery Barn Teen makes them and I am obsessed. (More to come on that). I got this one last week in the mail and it’s the perfect solution to having to sit on the cold, hard fireplace hearth. Now I can cozy up in a cushy beanbag! Aside from Neal rolling his eyes that “another fake dead animal showed up at our house while he was gone” the furry beanbag has been a welcome addition to the family. Last night was my Aunt Ann and Cousin Ally’s last night visiting us in Chicago! Neal’s mom and sister came over to meet them and it was so much fun! I made my mom’s “Christmas Eve Soup” (fun fact, I shared it as one of my first ever blog posts here if you want to see some REALLY bad photos and content. HAHA!) Anyway, speaking of cold. Have you started researching “Christmas Outfit Ideas” yet? I ask because, you know–experience. I always feel like I’m scrambling for festive attire right before a party or the day before Christmas Eve, and then I have to jump onto Pinterest to search “Christmas Outfit Ideas” and piece together something I already own. (I’m the worst procrastinator.) This shirt has always been a lifesaver in the winter because it’s the perfect party button-down. However, if you choose your pieces wisely, you can actually make them work for both work and play!

This is a staple that you’ll wear to death for every occasion. I love this top! It comes in tons of colors and will look beautiful with a pencil skirt for work, tucked into jean shorts for a casual Saturday, or with a mini skirt and OTK boots for a fall dinner date! Here are 12 fun gifts that help give back to those in need–gifts, I might add, that anyone would love to open on Christmas morning! Nest makes the most incredible smelling candles, and this one benefits an organization very near and dear to our hearts–Autism Speaks! I first discovered Bare soaps years back when I first started blogging! I absolutely LOVE all of their products! The company was founded with the goals of: 1. to educate and provide an all-natural product for those at home and 2. to create a sustainable sanitation program for the children in Kaberamaido, Uganda. They’ve seen so much success that they have expanded to benefit the Kalwa slum in India as well, providing women with fair wage jobs. The company also reinvests 20% of its profits to economic development. I love Kiehls products, as does Neal! Well guys, not sure if you’ve been experiencing the same this week, but FALL HAS ARRIVED.




(adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});

It’s cold, rainy, and hibernation mode has kicked in quite a few times this week. Luckily the forecast is supposed to take a warmer, sunnier turn over the next few days–so I can resume wearing this classic fall outfit of mine on repeat. Much to my fiancé’s (and your own significant others’) dismay–ITS TURTLENECK SEASON AGAIN! Super soft, thin turtlenecks are my very favorite things to wear. They might top the list as favorite wardrobe items. Neal, however, disagrees, referring to them as my “granny shirts.” (Which I do not take offense to, as my Granny was one of the coolest women to ever walk the earth and she also loved her turtlenecks. I suppose the turtleneck loving quality runs in the family.) Another fall wardrobe combo that will never go out of style: stripes and plaids. I don’t know what it is about them, but they’re like the peanut butter and jelly of my closet. When mixing any patterns, the general rule I follow is one small pattern + one larger pattern, so busy, thin stripes paired with a bold plaid works perfectly. My new favorite memory associated with this scarf is when we were up at the lake house recently, and Neal’s dad joked, “Jess, are you cold? I couldn’t help but notice the blanket you have wrapped around your throat.” I then proceeded to educate him on the concept of “blanket scarves”–he thought I was kidding. *Mind blown* (Noted on what to get him for Christmas.) Baha! Love him. Okay moving on–I couldn’t get through this post without talking about my favorite jacket in the whole world, could I? If you don’t yet own a Barbour Beadnell jacket, you’re truly missing out. It’s not too heavy, but very, very warm. I’m such a sucker for wardrobe classics (me? really?) and this is about as classic as they come. A Barbour coat will never go out of style, and it’s equally as practical as it is cute. It’s become my uniform paired with these jeans. (Are you getting sick of them yet? I can’t stop wearing them. I’ve tried.) Last but not least, the shoes! These pretties from Sole Society are the coolest color. Sometimes they’re reddish, sometimes they’re brownish, I don’t really care what color they are, because they add the perfect amount of spice to any outfit. I also wore them paired with this dress (majorly on sale!) for our engagement party last weekend–so cute!          Photos by Julie Kennedy Filed Under: Outfits, Style

Get this widget. Copyright© 2019 · Brunch Pro Theme by Shay Bocks The Golden Girl Chicago Fashion and Lifestyle Blog October 13, 2017   **Press play to watch the video!**  Happy Friday!! We’re back with our second post in the new Capsule Wardrobe Remix series! Today, we’re tackling the *not as tricky as you think* task of styling faux leather leggings in a versatile way. (I told you I’d prove to you that you can wear them tons of ways, didn’t I?!) I think that leather leggings are one of the more daunting trends out there right now. They seem a little hardcore at first glance. Sure, you know how to pull them off when going out to the bar with your girlfriends, but what about to a meeting? To a coffee date? To the airport? Or to brunch? Before we get into three ways to style them, let’s go over the items I styled with them here (you can also find the full list of all 21 October capsule items we talk about throughout this series here!) Leather leggings: First thing’s first, the star of today’s show! I’ve had mine for years, but I’ve heard amazing things about this Spanx pair in particular. (With a control top, even better!) Kelly and Shaheen swear by this control-top pair as well! This B.P. pair also has good reviews and is cheaper (just without control top!) Also, if you don’t want to commit to FULL faux leather leggings–I love this pair that just has one band of faux leather–so you get the effect but not the whole shebang, if you will. Leopard loafers: You’ll be seeing a LOT of these leopard loafers on this blog, because they really do make every outfit look instantly more stylish. Leopard always adds a ton of visual interest to any outfit, plus, they are truly the most comfortable shoes I have ever put on my feet. They required zero break-in, no blisters–ever! Heeled Booties: These booties by 1.State go with everything I own, they are SO comfy, and are only $99! I love the shape of the toe and the fact that they’re cut out in the back too, which adds a little more visual interest! Because of the shape and color, they also help to elongate your leg, which is hard to find in a bootie, as most of the time they can cut you off at the ankles and make your legs look stubby! (You also saw them worn in my outfit post earlier this week!) I also just got these booties from Bloomingdales that I’m obsessed with if you’re looking for a more classic style. White Sneakers: It’s no secret that I love my white sneakers. I’ve just about worn these Jack Purcells into the ground. Keds or white Converse are also great options. They are comfortable once you break them in and they look so classic, crisp, and timeless. They’re fantastic for travel and I often wear them to bop around the city on the weekends. Striped tee: I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again–when in doubt, choose a layer with stripes! I’ve found that classic black and white stripes add a lot more visual interest to your outfit than just a standard grey or white t-shirt. Plus, they look really cute mixed with other patterns, like leopard, or plaid! Again, mine featured here is old but this one is basically the exact same! I also love J.Crew’s striped “Perfect Tee.” White button down: Often, the classic white button down gets forgotten about once you’ve moved past that “first office job post college” phase–and it’s a shame! White button downs are one of my favorite layers all year round–they look adorable with jean shorts and just as cute layered under sweaters, over leather leggings, or tucked into boyfriend jeans. If you’re looking to look polished and classy but still chic and on-trend, this is one of the easiest ways to do it! Chunky cardigan: Another one you got a little glimpse of a few outfit posts back–this sweater by Free People (I also love this similar one) is so soft and cozy it’s to-die for! Cardigans are essentials in the fall and winter because of how easily you can throw them on over whatever you’re wearing–this one is great to keep at your desk or pull on when you wake up on a cool October morning! (Or…January morning, let’s be real. Haha!) Convertible sweater: This sweater, you guys, is probably one of the most versatile things you could buy this entire year. It’s both cowl neck and off the shoulder, you can wear it as a tunic or tuck it into high-waisted jeans or even a skirt. There are ENDLESS ways you can wear it and to top it off, it just might be one of the softest things I’ve ever purchased. (Oh, it comes in lot’s of colors too!) Leather tote: The Madewell Transport tote making the capsule wardrobe cut comes as a shock to absolutely none of you, I am sure. It’s my everything bag. Work, travel, groceries–whatever, this is always the bag I’m reaching for and it comes in several styles and colors as well. Plaid scarf: Of course, what fall wardrobe is complete without a plaid scarf? I love this one, this one, this one and this one, if you’re in the market for a new one! I love this one, this one, this one, and this one! Okay–now that we’ve gone over our essentials, let’s jump into how to style them, three ways! Great for a lunch meeting or post-work happy hour!      When I worked in advertising, outfits like this were my bread and butter! If you work in a similar environment that is more casual, yet still professional, you will get so much wear out of these. Why I love this combo: The crisp white button down makes it smart and classic for the office. It also accomplishes the task of covering your booty–which, as you can imagine, makes it more professional!) Going out afterwords? Tuck it in to make it feel more appropriate for a bar! The fact that the boots have heels also make them a bit more formal, without sacrificing comfort. I would spend what seemed like hours each week running back and forth from the creative department and down the halls in between meetings. Heeled booties with a thick heel were always my favorite–they never rubbed or killed my feet! (Great for a casual Friday at the office, or leisurely brunch!)   Fun trick: Always try to mix up and get creative with your layering. Often we think of layers as adding more over the top, but remember, you can always layer underneath, too. For example, the idea of wearing this cowl neck sweater with leather leggings might not feel creative. However, layering that white button down underneath, and adding a pop of leopard–does! This look would’ve been great for me for a casual Friday at the office, and it’s a perfect go-to outfit to hang out with friends–whether that be brunch, or to the movies–when you want to look pulled together but still want to feel like you’re in your pajamas! I also think leather leggings are a great essential for busy moms in particular because they are as easy to wear as regular leggings, but they are far more stylish and an easy way to make a statement. Also–perhaps an even bigger win: they don’t stain and are virtually food, stain, and liquid repellent!     A comfy + chic travel outfit!   I don’t know about you, but 99% of the time I am either dying of heat exhaustion or I feel like I’m sitting in an ice box at-risk for losing my toes. (I have bad circulation. My feet literally turn blue.) Anyway, that’s where–you guessed it–layers come in! A chunky cardigan like this one doesn’t just keep you warm, but it makes a stylish statement. A regular old cardigan just isn’t as exciting. It also adds in another fun textural element that this outfit would otherwise be lacking. This is why this outfit makes a perfect great go-to for travel (especially on airplanes where I want to die of cold.) By the way, this isn’t part of the capsule, but this suitcase is my favorite travel companion–I did a whole review on it here. Why this outfit works: you have a bit of pattern (stripes). You also have two different textures (chunky knit + faux leather). You’re also maintaining classic and flattering silhouettes! The leggings are high-rise and the shirt is tucked in. Both define the waist at it’s thinnest point and elongates the leg at the same time! The shoes also bring in a crisp, classic element and they’re a nice juxtaposition against the edgier leather leggings. (For a more “athleisure” type take, you can style this look with your favorite Nikes, and it would look just as cute!)
